definition_zh: 同事；同僚；（同一专业的）同行
definition_en: a person who works with you, especially one of the same rank, profession, or office
core_image: 两个人被同一份职责选中，并肩坐在同一张办公桌前
scene: 会议室里，两个人把同一份报告摊在桌上。 In the meeting room two colleagues spread the same report on the table and checked the figures line by line.
sceneCN: 这里 colleague 是「同事」（第 1 个义项：同一机构中的工作伙伴）；句意：会议室里，两位同事把同一份报告摊在桌上，逐条核对数据。

derivatives.zh: 同事间的；同僚式的；共享权力的
同僚平等共事的关系；同事间的和睦
学院；大学（同源于拉丁语 collegium“同受一职的团体”）
学院的；大学的；由同僚共同管理的

senses.title: The person beside you at work
senses.definition: a person who works with you in the same organization
senses.definitionCN: 在同一机构中与你一起工作的人
senses.example: I asked a colleague to cover my shift.
senses.exampleCN: 我请一位同事替我顶班。
senses.why: The Latin word named someone chosen together with you for one duty. The shared office is the everyday version of that joint appointment.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词本指“与你一同被选中承担同一职责的人”。今天共用一间办公室，就是那种“共同受命”的日常版本。

senses.title: Fellow member of a profession
senses.definition: a person in the same profession as you, especially in academic, medical, or legal settings
senses.definitionCN: 与你属于同一专业的人，尤用于学术、医疗或法律语境
senses.example: A colleague from the hospital reviewed the scan.
senses.exampleCN: 一位医院里的同行复核了这张扫描片。
senses.why: Here the bond is the profession rather than the payroll: two people are sent into the same field, even if they work in different buildings.
senses.whyCN: 这里把人连起来的是专业而不是工资单：两个人被送进同一个领域，即使不在同一栋楼里工作。

senses.title: Peer at another institution
senses.definition: a person doing the same kind of work elsewhere, treated as an equal in a wider network
senses.definitionCN: 在其他机构做同类工作、在更大网络中被视为平等同行的人
senses.example: She co-authored the paper with colleagues in Japan.
senses.exampleCN: 她与日本的同行合写了这篇论文。
senses.why: When the shared task is a field of research, the group stretches beyond one office; the colleague is still sent with you, only across a longer distance.
senses.whyCN: 当共同的任务是一片研究领域时，这个群体就越出了一间办公室；同行仍是“与你同被派出的人”，只是距离更远。

senses.title: One who shares an office or appointment
senses.definition: a person appointed to the same public office as another, especially in the Roman and later parliamentary tradition
senses.definitionCN: 与另一人被任命到同一公职的人，尤见于罗马及后来的议会传统
senses.example: In Rome, a consul governed together with a colleague.
senses.exampleCN: 在罗马，执政官要与一位同僚共同治理。
senses.why: This is the original scene: two men holding one office, each able to check the other. The word was born in that shared chair.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最初的场景：两个人共坐一个职位，彼此可以制衡。这个词就诞生于那把共享的椅子上。

senses.title: Partner on a joint task
senses.definition: a person working with you on a particular project rather than for the same employer
senses.definitionCN: 与你一起做某个具体项目、而不一定受雇于同一机构的人
senses.example: My colleague on the survey handled the interviews.
senses.exampleCN: 这个调查项目里与我合作的那位同事负责访谈。
senses.why: The task, not the institution, is what joins them. Remove the project and the relationship ends.
senses.whyCN: 把他们连起来的是任务而不是机构。项目一结束，这层关系也就结束了。

senses.title: Fellow member of a committee
senses.definition: a fellow member of a committee, board, or delegation
senses.definitionCN: 同一委员会、董事会或代表团的成员
senses.example: She briefed her colleagues on the board before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票前，她向董事会里的同僚做了简报。
senses.why: A committee is a body of people entrusted with one duty; its members are colleagues in the literal sense of sharing that charge.
senses.whyCN: 委员会是一群被托付同一职责的人；其成员就是字面意义上“共担这份托付”的同僚。

senses.title: Formal address in debate
senses.definition: a formal way of referring to another member in a parliament or assembly
senses.definitionCN: 在议会或会议上称呼另一位成员的正式说法
senses.example: The minister turned to her colleague across the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长转向过道对面的同僚。
senses.why: In debate the word keeps distance: it names the other as a fellow office-holder rather than as an opponent.
senses.whyCN: 在辩论中，这个词保持距离：它把对方称为“同样持有职位的人”，而不是“对手”。

senses.title: Collective staff
senses.definition: used in the plural, the employees of an organization regarded as a body
senses.definitionCN: 用复数形式，把某组织的全体员工视为一个整体
senses.example: The company told colleagues that the office would move.
senses.exampleCN: 公司通知全体员工，办公室要搬迁。
senses.why: A whole staff can be summed up as 'our colleagues', because every member stands in the same relation to the organization.
senses.whyCN: 整个员工队伍可以被统称为“我们的同事”，因为每个人与组织的关系都是一样的。

senses.title: Second opinion from a peer
senses.titleCN: 提供第二意见的平级同行
senses.definition: a person of the same rank consulted for professional judgment
senses.definitionCN: 被请来提供专业判断的同级人员
senses.example: He asked a colleague to look over the diagnosis.
senses.exampleCN: 他请一位同行再看一遍这个诊断。
senses.why: The shared rank is what makes the judgment trustworthy: the colleague is not above or below, but sent with you into the same problem.
senses.whyCN: 让这份判断可信的正是“同级”：这位同行不在你之上也不在你之下，而是与你一同被送进同一个难题。

intro.en: Colleague is a Latin political word before it is a workplace word: two people chosen together for one office. Dates are approximate, and the deeper origin of legare is disputed.
intro.cn: colleague 在成为“职场词”之前，先是一个拉丁语政治词：两个人一同被选中承担一个职位。年代为大致估计；legare 的更早来源存在争议。

items.en: Collega meant 'a partner in office, one chosen together with another'. It was used of consuls, tribunes and other magistrates who shared power.
items.cn: collega 意为“同僚、同被选中共担一职的人”，用于共享权力的执政官、保民官等官职。

items.en: com- 'together' + legare 'to send as a deputy, depute'. A colleague is literally a person sent together with you.
items.cn: 由 com-“一起”加 legare“作为代表派出、委任”构成。colleague 字面上就是“与你一同被派出的人”。

items.en: The same legare gives legate, delegate, delegation and legacy ('something handed on'). College and collegium belong to this group too, since a college is a body of people charged together.
items.cn: 同一个 legare 还给出 legate、delegate、delegation 和 legacy（“传下来的东西”）。college 与 collegium 也属于这一族，因为学院就是一群共同受托的人。

items.en: English borrowed colleague from Middle French collègue in the 1530s. Early uses still concerned offices and appointments rather than ordinary jobs.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪 30 年代从中古法语 collègue 借入。早期用法仍指官职与任命，而不是普通工作。

items.en: The word widened to any co-worker, then to professional peers in other institutions. Collective 'our colleagues' and the polite 'my colleague' in debate are later social extensions.
items.cn: 词义先扩大到任何同事，再扩大到其他机构的专业同行。统称“我们的同事”以及辩论中礼貌的“这位同僚”，都是后来社会用法的延伸。

items.en: Legare may go back to lex 'law' or to legere 'to choose, gather'; standard references do not settle the question, so the deepest link is source uncertain.
items.cn: legare 可能追溯到 lex“法律”，也可能追溯到 legere“挑选、聚集”；通行资料并未定论，故最深层联系来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: an institution of higher education, or a body of people with a shared duty. It comes from the same Latin collegium.
entries.definitionCN: 学院；高等学校；也指共同承担职责的团体。它来自同一个拉丁词 collegium。

entries.definition: a picture made by pasting pieces onto a surface. It sounds close but comes from French coller 'to glue'.
entries.definitionCN: 拼贴画。读音相近，但来自法语 coller“粘贴”，与“同僚”无关。

entries.definition: shared among peers, or marked by equal colleagues. It is the adjective built on colleague.
entries.definitionCN: 同僚共享的；同僚式的。它是由 colleague 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a person who works in the same place as you. It is the plain everyday word and says nothing about rank or profession.
entries.definitionCN: 同事。最日常的说法，不涉及级别或专业。

entries.definition: a person connected with you in business or work, often at a similar level. It is more formal and more commercial than colleague.
entries.definitionCN: 同事；业务伙伴。比 colleague 更正式、更偏商业，常指地位相近者。

entries.definition: a person of the same age, status, or ability as you. It stresses equality rather than shared employment.
entries.definitionCN: 同辈；同级者。强调同等地位，而不是同属一个单位。

entries.definition: a person who shares an activity or business with you. It stresses the joint venture rather than the office.
entries.definitionCN: 搭档；合伙人。强调共同做事或共同经营，而不是同处一间办公室。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin pieces com- and legare, the shared family of delegate and college, and the settings in which English actually uses the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁成分 com- 与 legare、delegate 与 college 的同一词族，以及英语里实际使用这个词的场景。

normal.en: colleague = com- 'together' + legare 'send': a person sent together with you, not above you and not below you.
normal.cn: colleague = com-“一起”+ legare“派出”：一个与你一同被派出的人，既不在你之上，也不在你之下。

normal.en: Delegate and colleague share legare: a delegate is sent down to a task, a colleague is sent alongside you.
normal.cn: delegate 与 colleague 共享 legare：delegate 是被派下去办一件事，colleague 是被派到你身边同行。

normal.en: College belongs to the same family: a college is first a body of people charged together, then the place where they work.
normal.cn: college 属于同一词族：它先是“一群共同受托的人”，然后才指这群人工作的场所。

normal.en: In parliament, 'my colleague' is a polite label that keeps the other member at a professional distance.
normal.cn: 在议会里，“my colleague”是一种礼貌标签，把对方保持在职业距离之外。

normal.en: A collegial department is one where colleagues treat each other as equals rather than as a chain of command.
normal.cn: a collegial department 指同僚以平等相待、而非按命令链条运作的部门。

abstract.en: The image is two chairs at one desk: the same duty has been assigned to two people, so neither owns the desk alone.
abstract.cn: 意象是一张桌子旁的两把椅子：同一份职责被交给两个人，所以谁也不能独占这张桌子。

abstract.en: Distance does not break the word: the same 'sent with' relation reaches across campuses and countries.
abstract.cn: 距离并不会切断这个词：同一种“与你同被派出”的关系可以跨校园、跨国界。

abstract.en: The word is about rank as much as place: a colleague is a peer, which is why a second opinion from one carries weight.
abstract.cn: 这个词既讲场所也讲级别：colleague 是平级者，所以来自同行的第二意见才有分量。

examples.en: I share an office with two colleagues from the design team.
examples.cn: 我和设计团队的两位同事共用一间办公室。

examples.en: Several colleagues from other universities joined the workshop.
examples.cn: 来自其他大学的几位同行参加了这次研讨班。

examples.en: She asked a colleague to check the figures before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前，她请一位同事核对了这些数字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「考立格」——考场里立在旁边的格子衫大哥，是天天一起干活的同事 → colleague 同事

root: 源自拉丁语 collega“同僚”，由 com-“一起”+ legare“作为代表派出”构成，字面意思是“与你一同被派出的人”，核心是“同级共事”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of colleague, all built on one relation: being sent together into the same duty. The duty can be an office, an employer, a profession, a project, a committee, or a single diagnosis.
sensesIntro.cn: colleague 的九个义项都建立在同一种关系上：被一同派进同一份职责。这份职责可以是一个官职、一家单位、一个专业、一个项目、一个委员会，甚至一次诊断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people placed together in one duty, side by side rather than one above the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人被放进同一份职责里，并肩而立，而不是一人高一人低。

branches.en: SAME WORKPLACE: one desk-mate is a colleague, and the whole staff can be addressed as colleagues.
branches.cn: 同一职场：同桌办公的人是同事，整支员工队伍也可以被统称为同事。

branches.en: SAME PROFESSION: the bond survives a change of building, so a doctor or researcher has colleagues across the city and across the world.
branches.cn: 同一专业：换了楼也不会断这层关系，所以医生或研究者在本市、在全世界都有同行。

branches.en: SHARED APPOINTMENT: the original sense survives in shared public office, in boards and committees, and in the formal language of debate.
branches.cn: 共担任命：原义保存在共任公职、董事会与委员会，以及辩论的正式措辞里。

branches.en: SHARED TASK: a project can create colleagues for its duration, even without a common employer.
branches.cn: 共担任务：一个项目就能在存续期间造出“同事”，即使没有共同雇主。

branches.en: SHARED JUDGMENT: equality of rank is what makes a colleague's second opinion worth asking for.
branches.cn: 共担判断：正因为级别相同，同行的第二意见才值得请教。

intro.en: Colleague is a complete Latin noun rather than an English prefix-plus-root construction. English adds only suffixes, while legare supplies a whole family of sending and delegating words.
intro.cn: colleague 是一个完整的拉丁名词，而不是英语“前缀加词根”的构造。英语只在其后加后缀；legare 则提供了整族表示“派出、委托”的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family rests on legare 'to send as a deputy': collega, legatus, delegare and collegium. Through these, English also gets legate, delegate, legacy and college.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族以 legare“作为代表派出”为核心：collega、legatus、delegare、collegium。经由这些词，英语也得到了 legate、delegate、legacy 和 college。

items.meaning: a person sent together with you into the same office
items.meaningCN: 同事；同僚（com- 表“一起”，legare 表“派出”，-a 为名词词尾）
items.example: My colleague handled the client call.
items.exampleCN: 我的同事处理了那通客户电话。

items.meaning: of or shared among colleagues; marked by equal partnership
items.meaningCN: 同僚间的；同僚式的（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: The faculty runs on collegial decision-making.
items.exampleCN: 这个学院靠同僚共同决策来运转。

items.meaning: the quality of working as equals among colleagues
items.meaningCN: 同僚平等共事的关系（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: Collegiality is valued in the department.
items.exampleCN: 这个系很看重同僚间的平等氛围。

items.meaning: the state or relationship of being colleagues
items.meaningCN: 同事关系；同僚情谊（-ship 表示状态或关系）
items.example: Years of colleagueship made the handover easy.
items.exampleCN: 多年的同事情谊让交接变得顺利。

items.meaning: a body of people charged with one duty; later, the place where they work
items.meaningCN: 共同受托的团体；后指学院（拉丁 collegium 的英语形式）
items.example: She teaches at a small college.
items.exampleCN: 她在一所小学院任教。

items.meaning: relating to a college, or shared by a body of equals
items.meaningCN: 学院的；由同僚共同管理的（-ate 构成形容词）
items.example: The university has a collegiate government.
items.exampleCN: 这所大学实行同僚共同治理。

items.meaning: to send someone to act for you; a person so sent
items.meaningCN: 委派；代表（de- 表“派出”，legare 表“送”，同一词根）
items.example: She delegated the task to a junior staffer.
items.exampleCN: 她把这项任务委派给一位年轻职员。

items.meaning: a group sent to represent others; the act of sending them
items.meaningCN: 代表团；委派（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: A trade delegation visited the port.
items.exampleCN: 一个贸易代表团参观了港口。

items.meaning: an official envoy, especially a papal representative
items.meaningCN: 使节；教廷使节（同一词根，指被派出的人）
items.example: The legate carried a letter from Rome.
items.exampleCN: 使节带着一封来自罗马的信。

items.meaning: something handed down from the past
items.meaningCN: 遗产；遗留（legare 的“传下去”义 + -acy）
items.example: The library is part of his legacy.
items.exampleCN: 这座图书馆是他遗产的一部分。

latinEntries.meaning: to send as a deputy; to bequeath
a body of colleagues sharing one office
latinEntries.meaningCN: 同僚团体；共同任职的机构

definition_zh: 结合；联合；混合；兼有；联合收割机；联合企业
definition_en: to join two or more things so that they become one, or to do two things at the same time
core_image: 把两束麦秆并成一把，用同一根绳捆住
scene: 两家小公司的门牌挂在同一层楼，实验室还很空。 The two small firms decided to combine their research teams and share one laboratory.
sceneCN: 这里 combine 是「合并、联合」（第 3 个义项：把人员或机构合到一起）；句意：两家小公司决定把研究团队合并起来，共用一间实验室。

collocations.zh: 把 A 与 B 结合起来

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Join two things into one
senses.definition: to join two or more separate things so that they form one whole
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多分开的事物连成一个整体
senses.example: Combine the two short reports into a single document.
senses.exampleCN: 把这两份短报告合并成一份文件。
senses.why: The Latin word is built on bini 'two by two'. The basic act is pairing: two things are laid together until the pair counts as one.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词建立在 bini“两个两个地”上。最基本的动作就是配对：把两样东西摆到一起，直到这一对算作一个。

senses.title: Mix substances together
senses.definition: to mix two or more substances so that they are blended
senses.definitionCN: 把两种或更多物质混合、搅匀
senses.example: Combine the flour and butter until the mixture looks like crumbs.
senses.exampleCN: 把面粉和黄油混合，直到混合物呈碎屑状。
senses.why: When the pair being joined is flour and butter, the result is not two objects side by side but one new texture. Mixing is pairing taken to the point of blending.
senses.whyCN: 当被合起来的是面粉和黄油，结果不是并排的两样东西，而是一种新的质地。混合就是把“配对”做到彼此交融的程度。

senses.title: Unite people or organizations
senses.titleCN: 把人员或机构联合起来
senses.definition: to unite people, groups, or companies so that they act as one
senses.definitionCN: 把人员、团体或公司联合起来，使其作为一个整体行动
senses.example: The two firms combined their research teams.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家公司合并了各自的研究团队。
senses.why: The paired units here are whole teams. Joining them pools separate efforts into one force, which is why combine usually implies cooperation rather than conquest.
senses.whyCN: 这里配对的是整支团队。把它们合起来，就是把分散的力量汇成一股，因此 combine 通常暗示合作，而不是征服。

senses.title: Have two qualities at once
senses.definition: to possess two or more qualities or roles at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 同时具备两种或更多特质或身份
senses.example: The design combines simplicity with strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计兼具简洁与坚固。
senses.why: Not every union is physical. Two qualities can be held in one object, so combining becomes 'carrying both at once' rather than 'putting together'.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有结合都是物理的。两种特质可以存在同一个物体里，于是 combine 变成“同时兼具”，而不是“拼到一起”。

senses.title: Chemical combination
senses.definition: of atoms or substances, to unite chemically to form a new substance
senses.definitionCN: （原子或物质）经化学作用结合成新物质
senses.example: Hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water.
senses.exampleCN: 氢与氧化合生成水。
senses.why: Chemistry picks the strictest version of pairing: the parts lose their separate identity and a compound appears. The everyday word is used for a change that cannot simply be undone.
senses.whyCN: 化学取用了“配对”最严格的版本：各成分失去独立身份，生成一种化合物。日常词在这里指一种不能简单还原的变化。

senses.title: Become one by itself
senses.definition: of separate streams, paths, or groups, to merge into one
senses.definitionCN: （分流、道路或群体）自行汇合成一个
senses.example: The two trails combine just above the waterfall.
senses.exampleCN: 两条小径在瀑布上方汇合。
senses.why: No outside hand is needed here: the two things move toward each other and become one. The verb turns intransitive, describing the meeting point rather than the joiner.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要外力的手：两样东西自行靠近、成为一个。动词转为不及物，描述的是汇合点，而不是“合并者”。

senses.title: The combine harvester
senses.definition: a machine that cuts and threshes grain in one operation
senses.definitionCN: 一次完成收割与脱粒的机械
senses.example: One combine harvested the whole field in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一台联合收割机一天就收完了整块田。
senses.why: The machine is named for combining two jobs that used to need separate crews. The noun keeps the verb's promise: two operations become one pass.
senses.whyCN: 这台机器因“合并”了两项原本需要不同人手的工序而得名。名词保留了动词的承诺：两道工序变成一趟作业。

senses.title: A commercial combine
senses.definition: a group of companies or interests acting together as one organization
senses.definitionCN: 多家公司或利益方联合运作的组织
senses.example: The paper mills formed a combine to control prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这些造纸厂组成一个联合企业来操控价格。
senses.why: When the paired units are firms, the union itself becomes a thing with a name. This noun often carries a suspicious tone, because a combine can shut out competition.
senses.whyCN: 当配对单位是公司时，这个联合本身就成了一个有名字的实体。这个名词常带警惕意味，因为联合企业可能排挤竞争。

senses.title: Combined: taken together
senses.definition: the past participle used as an adjective, meaning joint or total
senses.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，表示“联合的、合起来算的”
senses.example: The combined weight of the two boxes broke the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 两个箱子合起来的重量压塌了架子。
senses.why: Once the parts are joined, they can be counted as one sum. The participle freezes the completed union into a description.
senses.whyCN: 部件一旦合起来，就可以按一个总数来算。过去分词把完成的联合凝固成一种描述。

intro.en: Combine comes from a Late Latin verb meaning 'to unite two by two'. Its history is short and clear on the 'two' element, less clear on the farming and business nouns.
intro.cn: combine 来自一个意为“两个两个地合起来”的晚期拉丁语动词。它的历史不复杂：“二”的成分很清楚，农业与商业名词的出现时间则较模糊。

items.en: Combinare meant 'to unite, yoke together'. It was formed from com- 'together' plus bini 'two by two', from bis 'twice'.
items.cn: combinare 意为“联合、套在一起”，由 com-“一起”加 bini“两个两个地”（源于 bis“两次”）构成。

items.en: The verb passed into Medieval Latin and French as a general word for joining. The image of yoking a pair of animals remained underneath.
items.cn: 这个动词进入中世纪拉丁语和法语，成为表示“连接”的一般动词。底下仍保留着“把一对牲口套上轭”的意象。

items.en: Old French combiner (14c.) meant 'to join, unite'. It was used of people and things alike, without the chemical or mechanical senses.
items.cn: 古法语 combiner（14 世纪）意为“连接、联合”，人和物都可用，尚无化学或机械义。

items.en: English adopted combine in the 15th century. The 'mix substances' sense and the 'unite forces' sense both appear early, since both are versions of joining.
items.cn: 英语于 15 世纪借入 combine。“混合物质”与“联合力量”两义都出现得很早，因为二者都只是“连接”的不同版本。

items.en: The business combine ('association of firms') is recorded in the 19th century. The combine harvester is a 20th-century name for a machine that performs two jobs at once.
items.cn: 商业义“联合企业”记录于 19 世纪；combine harvester（联合收割机）是 20 世纪的名称，指一次完成两道工序的机器。

items.en: Bis and bini go back to PIE *dwo- 'two', the same source as duo, dual and twin. The reconstructed root is not attested, so the deepest step is source uncertain.
items.cn: bis 与 bini 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dwo-“二”，与 duo、dual、twin 同源。重构词根没有书面记录，故最深层来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the act or result of joining things. It is the noun built directly on combine.
entries.definitionCN: 结合；组合；结合物。它是直接由 combine 构成的名词。

entries.definition: joint or total, as in 'combined efforts'. It is the past participle used as an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 联合的；合计的，如 combined efforts。它是过去分词作形容词。

entries.definition: a machine that reaps and threshes in one pass. The noun keeps the verb's 'two jobs in one' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 联合收割机。这个名词保留了动词“两道工序合成一道”的意思。

entries.definition: fighting or struggle. It shares the com- opening but comes from a different root meaning 'to strike'.
entries.definitionCN: 战斗；搏斗。同样以 com- 开头，但词根不同，意为“打击”。

entries.definition: to join or blend into a single whole, especially of companies or streams. It stresses the disappearance of the boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 合并；汇合。强调界线消失，尤用于公司或水流。

entries.definition: to join people or groups for a common purpose. It is more purposeful and often more emotional than combine.
entries.definitionCN: 联合；团结。比 combine 更强调共同目标，也常带情感色彩。

entries.definition: to mix things so that they are no longer distinct. It is the natural word for colours, teas, and flavours.
entries.definitionCN: 混合；调和。强调混合后分辨不出原来的成分，常用于颜色、茶与味道。

entries.definition: to bring parts into a working whole. It stresses that the parts still function together after joining.
entries.definitionCN: 整合；使一体化。强调各部分结合后仍协同运作。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin bini 'two by two', the -ate verb suffix, and the English nouns for the machine and the business group.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 bini“两个两个地”、动词后缀 -ate，以及指机器与商业集团的英语名词。

normal.en: combine = com- 'together' + bini 'two by two': first you pair things, then the pair counts as one.
normal.cn: combine = com-“一起”+ bini“两个两个地”：先配对，再让这一对算作一个。

normal.en: Combination is the everyday noun: a combination lock works because several dials must line up as one pattern.
normal.cn: combination 是日常名词：密码锁能开，是因为几个转盘必须合成同一个图案。

normal.en: A combine harvester combines two jobs, cutting and threshing, which used to need separate crews.
normal.cn: combine harvester 合并了两道工序，收割与脱粒，过去这两样需要不同的人手。

normal.en: Combine forces is the political and military phrase: separate units pool their strength into one push.
normal.cn: combine forces 是政治与军事用语：分开的单位把力量汇成一次推进。

normal.en: In chemistry, combine is the strongest form: the parts do not sit side by side, they form a new substance.
normal.cn: 在化学里，combine 是最强的形式：各成分不是并排放着，而是生成一种新物质。

abstract.en: The core picture is a bundle: two sheaves are laid together and tied with one cord, so the cord now holds a single object.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一捆东西：两束麦秆并到一起，用同一根绳捆住，于是绳子握住的成了一个物体。

abstract.en: The two become one in different degrees: side by side, blended, chemically fused, or merely counted as a total.
abstract.cn: “两成一”有不同的程度：并排、混合、化学熔合，或者仅仅合起来计数。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from matter to people: what can be tied can also be teamed.
abstract.cn: 这个词能从物质轻松转到人：能被捆在一起的东西，也能被组成一队。

examples.en: The recipe tells you to combine the eggs and sugar first.
examples.cn: 食谱要求先把鸡蛋和糖混合。

examples.en: The two universities combined their libraries into one digital catalogue.
examples.cn: 两所大学把各自的图书馆合并成一个数字目录。

examples.en: Her job combines teaching with research.
examples.cn: 她的工作兼有教学与研究。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯拜」——肯拜把子的两伙人，最后合成一队 → combine 结合、联合

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 combinare“联合、套在一起”，由 com-“一起”+ bini“两个两个地”（bis“两次”）构成，核心是“把两样并成一样”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of combine, all starting from pairing. Two objects, two substances, two teams, two qualities, two atoms, two streams, two farm jobs, two companies, and finally two amounts counted as one.
sensesIntro.cn: combine 的九个义项都从“配对”出发：两件物品、两种材料、两支团队、两种特质、两个原子、两道水流、两道农活、两家公司，最后是两笔数量合起来算。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things laid together and held by one cord, so that the pair now counts as one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西摆到一起，被同一根绳握住，于是这一对现在算作一个。

branches.en: MATTER JOINED: documents are stapled into one file, and flour and butter become one dough.
branches.cn: 物质相合：文件被订成一份，面粉与黄油变成一团面团。

branches.en: GROUPS MEET: teams are pooled by someone, while streams and trails merge by themselves.
branches.cn: 群体相遇：团队由人合并，水流与小径则自行汇合。

branches.en: ONE THING, TWO COUNTS: an object can carry two qualities, and joined parts can be added up as a total.
branches.cn: 一物两算：一个物体可以兼具两种特质，合起来的部分也可以按总数相加。

branches.en: ATOMS FUSE: chemistry uses the strictest union, where the parts become a new substance.
branches.cn: 原子熔合：化学用的是最严格的联合，各成分变成一种新物质。

branches.en: TWO JOBS, ONE NAME: the harvester merges two farm operations, and the business combine merges separate firms.
branches.cn: 两件事，一个名字：收割机合并两道农活，联合企业合并多家公司。

intro.en: Combine is built from Latin pieces that are easy to see: com- 'together', the numeral base bini 'two by two', and the verb suffix -ate. English derivatives add -ation, -ed, -able, -al and -er.
intro.cn: combine 由几个在英语里容易看出的拉丁成分构成：com-“一起”、数词基 bini“两个两个地”、动词后缀 -ate。英语派生词再加上 -ation、-ed、-able、-al、-er。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is small and numerical: bini and bis 'twice' supply the 'two' idea, while combinare supplies the joining. Binary is the close cousin through bini, and binomial repeats the same 'two' idea with the prefix bi-.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族小而偏数词：bini 与 bis“两次”提供“二”的概念，combinare 提供“连接”。binary 是经由 bini 的近亲，binomial 则用前缀 bi- 重复同一个“二”的概念。

items.meaning: to join a pair into one
items.meaningCN: 结合；联合（com- 表“一起”，bini 表“两个两个地”，-ate 构成动词）
items.example: Combine the two files before sending them.
items.exampleCN: 发送前把两个文件合并起来。

items.meaning: the act of joining, or the joined result
items.meaningCN: 结合；组合；结合物（-ation 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The dish is a combination of rice and beans.
items.exampleCN: 这道菜是米饭和豆子的组合。

items.meaning: joined together; counted as a total
items.meaningCN: 联合的；合计的（-ed 构成过去分词或形容词）
items.example: The combined sales reached a million.
items.exampleCN: 合计销售额达到一百万。

items.meaning: able to be joined or mixed
items.meaningCN: 可结合的；可混合的（-able 表“能够被……”）
items.example: These two chemicals are combinable under heat.
items.exampleCN: 这两种化学品在加热条件下可以化合。

items.meaning: relating to combinations; in logic, built from combined gates
items.meaningCN: 组合的；（逻辑）组合式的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: A combinational circuit has no memory.
items.exampleCN: 组合逻辑电路没有记忆功能。

items.meaning: one that combines, such as a device merging signals
items.meaningCN: 合并者；组合器（-er 表示做动作的人或装置）
items.example: The signal combiner merges two antenna feeds.
items.exampleCN: 信号合并器把两路天线输入合在一起。

items.meaning: consisting of two parts; using two digits
items.meaningCN: 二元的；二进制的（同一“二”词根 + -ary）
items.example: Computers store data in binary form.
items.exampleCN: 计算机以二进制形式存储数据。

items.meaning: an expression or name with two terms
items.meaningCN: 二项式；双名（bi-“二”+ 希腊语 nomos“名称”）
items.example: Biologists use a binomial name for each species.
items.exampleCN: 生物学家为每个物种使用双名。

definition_zh: 开始；着手；开始存在；（仪式）开始
definition_en: to begin, especially in a formal or official way
core_image: 推开一扇门，跨过门槛，让一件事正式起步
scene: 奠基仪式上，铁锹落下第一铲土。 The first spadeful of soil was turned, and the construction work commenced.
sceneCN: 这里 commence 是「正式开始」（第 2 个义项：仪式或工程按程序启动）；句意：第一铲土落下，工程正式开始了。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Begin an activity
senses.definition: to begin doing something, especially something planned or formal
senses.definitionCN: 开始做某事，尤指有计划或正式的事
senses.example: The meeting will commence at nine sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 会议将于九点整开始。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind it means 'to go in, enter'. To commence is to step across a threshold into an activity that now counts as begun.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的拉丁动词意为“走入、进入”。commence 就是跨过一道门槛，进入一件从此算作“已开始”的事。

senses.title: Start a ceremony or formal event
senses.definition: of a ceremony, ceremony, or public event, to open in the prescribed way
senses.definitionCN: （典礼或公共活动）按既定程序开场
senses.example: The graduation ceremony commenced with the national anthem.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在国歌声中开始。
senses.why: Formal events have a marked entrance. Commence is the word for that moment when the ceremony leaves the waiting state and officially runs.
senses.whyCN: 正式活动有一个明确的“入场点”。commence 就指典礼离开等待状态、正式开始运转的那一刻。

senses.title: Take effect legally
senses.definition: of a contract, lease, or rule, to begin to have legal force
senses.definitionCN: （合同、租约或规则）开始具有法律效力
senses.example: The lease commences on the first of May.
senses.exampleCN: 租约自五月一日起生效。
senses.why: A contract also has a threshold: before a stated date it exists on paper but does nothing. Commencing is the moment it starts to bind the parties.
senses.whyCN: 合同也有一道门槛：在约定日期之前，它只在纸上存在，并不起作用。commence 就是它开始约束各方的时刻。

senses.title: Come into existence
senses.definition: of an era, process, or state, to begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: （时代、过程或状态）开始存在
senses.example: A new era of trade commenced after the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 条约签订后，贸易的新时代开始了。
senses.why: Here nothing is literally done by a person: a period opens. The verb describes the first point of a stretch of time rather than a first action.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不是某个人在做动作，而是一段时期打开了。动词描述的是时间段的第一个点，而不是第一个动作。

senses.title: Commence work or duty
senses.definition: to start work, duty, or a job, especially on a fixed date
senses.definitionCN: 开始工作、履职或上任，尤指在某个固定日期
senses.example: She commences duty as head nurse next Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 她下周一正式出任护士长。
senses.why: A post is a role someone enters. The word marks the crossing from appointee to office-holder, which is why it suits official appointments.
senses.whyCN: 职位是人“进入”的角色。这个词标记了从“被任命者”到“在职者”的跨越，因此适合正式任命。

senses.title: Commencement: the graduation ceremony
senses.definition: the noun commencement, in American English, the ceremony at which degrees are awarded
senses.definitionCN: 名词 commencement，在美式英语中指授予学位的毕业典礼
senses.example: Parents flew in for commencement.
senses.exampleCN: 父母专程飞来参加毕业典礼。
senses.why: The ceremony marks not the end of study but the beginning of the next stage. The noun keeps the verb's forward-facing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个典礼标记的不是学业的结束，而是下一阶段的开始。这个名词保留了动词“朝前看”的含义。

senses.title: Commence proceedings
senses.definition: to begin a legal action or official procedure
senses.definitionCN: 开始法律诉讼或正式程序
senses.example: The tenant commenced proceedings against the landlord.
senses.exampleCN: 租客对房东提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Legal procedure is a sequence with a formal first step. Commencing names that step, so the phrase is fixed in court language.
senses.whyCN: 法律程序是一套有正式第一步的序列。commence 命名了那一步，因此这个搭配在法庭语言里是固定的。

senses.title: Commencing: opening or initial
senses.definition: the present participle used attributively, meaning opening or initial
senses.definitionCN: 现在分词作定语，表示“开端的、起初的”
senses.example: The commencing chapter sets out the main argument.
senses.exampleCN: 开篇那一章提出了主要论点。
senses.why: The participle captures the first moment as it happens. Used before a noun, it labels whatever stands at the entrance of a sequence.
senses.whyCN: 现在分词捕捉正在发生的“第一刻”。放在名词前，它就标注处于序列入口的那个东西。

intro.en: Commence is a French-shaped verb built on a Latin beginning. The 'entering' image is visible in its Latin ancestors, and the graduation sense is an American development.
intro.cn: commence 是一个法语形的动词，建立在拉丁语“开始”之上。“进入”的意象在其拉丁语祖先里看得见，毕业典礼义则是美式英语的发展。

items.en: Initium meant 'a beginning', and inire meant 'to go in, enter, begin'. The physical image is stepping inside.
items.cn: initium 意为“开端”，inire 意为“走入、进入、开始”。其具体意象是“迈步进入”。

items.en: A reconstructed *cominitiare added com- 'together' as an intensifier to initiare 'to begin'. The com- does not mean 'with someone' here; it strengthens the start.
items.cn: 重构形式 *cominitiare 在 initiare“开始”前加了加强语气的 com-。这里的 com- 不是“与人一起”，而是强化“开始”这一动作。

items.en: Old French comencier, commencier (11c.) carried the word into everyday French with the sense 'to begin'.
items.cn: 古法语 comencier、commencier（11 世纪）把这个词带入日常法语，意为“开始”。

items.en: English took commence from French in the 14th century. It has always sounded more formal than begin, which is native English.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪从法语借入 commence。它一直比本族语的 begin 更正式。

items.en: Commencement for the degree ceremony is a 19th-century American usage. The idea is that the ceremony begins the graduate's new life rather than closing their studies.
items.cn: 用 commencement 指学位授予典礼，是 19 世纪的美式用法。其理据是：典礼开启毕业生的新生活，而不是结束学业。

items.en: Modern usage keeps commence for ceremonies, contracts, works, and legal proceedings. Begin and start cover the ordinary, informal cases.
items.cn: 现代用法把 commence 留给典礼、合同、工程与法律程序；日常非正式场合则由 begin 和 start 承担。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the buying and selling of goods. It shares the comm- opening but comes from merx 'merchandise', not from 'begin'.
entries.definitionCN: 商业；贸易。同样以 comm- 开头，但来自 merx“商品”，与“开始”无关。

entries.definition: a remark or explanation. It shares the opening syllables but comes from a verb meaning 'to devise, think'.
entries.definitionCN: 评论；说明。开头音节相近，但来自意为“构思、思考”的动词。

entries.definition: to praise or recommend. It is close in sound but means handing something over with approval.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；推荐。读音接近，但意思是带着认可把某物交出去。

entries.definition: a beginning, or the graduation ceremony. It is the noun built directly on commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；毕业典礼。它是直接由 commence 构成的名词。

entries.definition: to start doing something. It is the ordinary native word, with no special formality.
entries.definitionCN: 开始。最普通的本族词，不带正式色彩。

entries.definition: to begin, often with a sense of setting something in motion. It is more physical and less ceremonial than commence.
entries.definitionCN: 开始；启动。更偏“让某物动起来”，不如 commence 正式。

entries.definition: to cause a process to begin. It stresses the first push rather than the ceremony of opening.
entries.definitionCN: 发起；启动。强调最初的一推，而不是开场仪式。

entries.definition: to start something publicly, especially a product or campaign. It adds publicity to the beginning.
entries.definitionCN: 正式推出；发起。在“开始”之外增加了公开宣传的意味。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin initium 'beginning', the French form of the verb, and the fixed phrases in which English still prefers commence.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 initium“开端”、该动词的法语形式，以及英语仍偏好用 commence 的固定搭配。

normal.en: commence and initiate are cousins: both sit on Latin initium 'a beginning', which pictures a person stepping inside.
normal.cn: commence 与 initiate 是远亲：两者都建立在拉丁语 initium“开端”上，意象是“人迈步进入”。

normal.en: Commence is the formal twin of begin: meetings, ceremonies, contracts and court proceedings commence.
normal.cn: commence 是 begin 的正式孪生兄弟：会议、典礼、合同与法庭程序都用 commence。

normal.en: A lease commences on a date, because the contract crosses its threshold at that moment.
normal.cn: 租约在某日 commence，因为合同就在那一刻跨过自己的门槛。

normal.en: Commencement is the American graduation ceremony: it opens the next stage rather than closing the school years.
normal.cn: commencement 是美式毕业典礼：它开启下一阶段，而不是给学校岁月画句号。

normal.en: Commencing work means crossing from preparation into production, which is why factories and sites use the word.
normal.cn: commencing work 指从准备跨入生产，因此工厂与工地爱用这个词。

abstract.en: The core picture is a door: the activity already exists behind it, and commence is the act of stepping through.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一扇门：活动早就在门后存在，commence 是跨过去的那一步。

abstract.en: The word always looks forward: what is commencing is not the old state but the new one that has just been entered.
abstract.cn: 这个词总是朝前看：正在 commence 的不是旧状态，而是刚刚被进入的新状态。

abstract.en: Formality is the word's social dress: the same threshold is crossed by begin in speech and by commence in documents.
abstract.cn: 正式性是这个词的社会外衣：同一道门槛，口语用 begin 跨，文件用 commence 跨。

examples.en: Construction will commence as soon as the permit is issued.
examples.cn: 许可证一经签发，工程就会开工。

examples.en: The course commences with a short diagnostic test.
examples.cn: 这门课以一次简短的诊断测试开始。

examples.en: Her contract commences in September and runs for two years.
examples.cn: 她的合同九月生效，为期两年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可门寺」——寺门一开，法会正式开始 → commence 开始

root: 源自拉丁语 initium“开端”、inire“走入、开始”，经俗拉丁语 *cominitiare 与古法语 comencier 进入英语，核心是“跨进门、正式起步”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of commence, all organised around a threshold. An activity, a ceremony, a contract, an era, a post, a degree ceremony, a lawsuit, and an opening chapter each have their own moment of stepping through.
sensesIntro.cn: commence 的八个义项都围绕一道门槛组织：一项活动、一场典礼、一份合同、一个时代、一个职位、一次毕业典礼、一场诉讼、开篇一章，各自都有跨过去的那一刻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door already open, and the step that carries someone across the threshold.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇已经打开的门，以及把人带过门槛的那一步。

branches.en: THE FIRST STEP: an activity or a first chapter is what lies just inside the door.
branches.cn: 第一步：门内最近的东西，是一项活动或开篇一章。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC OPENING: ceremonies and graduations are entrances performed in front of others.
branches.cn: 公开开场：典礼与毕业式是在众人面前完成的“入场”。

branches.en: FORMAL FORCE: a contract or a lawsuit starts to bind only when its stated threshold is crossed.
branches.cn: 正式效力：合同或诉讼只有跨过既定门槛，才开始产生约束力。

branches.en: A PERIOD OPENS: an era commences without any person acting, because time itself is the thing that starts.
branches.cn: 时期开启：时代自行 commence，无需某个人动手，因为开始的是时间本身。

branches.en: A ROLE BEGINS: taking up a post is entering a chair that already exists.
branches.cn: 角色开始：上任就是进入一把早已存在的椅子。

intro.en: Commence carries the Latin beginning initium inside it. English adds -ment to make the noun and -ing to make the participle; the prefix com- here only intensifies.
intro.cn: commence 内部携带着拉丁语“开端”initium。英语加 -ment 构成名词，加 -ing 构成分词；这里的 com- 只起加强语气作用。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family around initium is large and still productive in English: initial, initiative, initiate, initiation, and the verb inire 'to go in'.
latinIntro.cn: 围绕 initium 的拉丁词族很大，在英语里仍有生产力：initial、initiative、initiate、initiation，以及动词 inire“走入”。

items.meaning: to begin formally
items.meaningCN: 开始；正式着手（com- 表加强，initiare 表“开始”）
items.example: The hearing commences tomorrow.
items.exampleCN: 听证会明天开始。

items.meaning: a beginning; a graduation ceremony
items.meaningCN: 开始；毕业典礼（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: Commencement is held on the main lawn.
items.exampleCN: 毕业典礼在主草坪上举行。

items.meaning: opening, initial
items.meaningCN: 开端的；起初的（-ing 构成现在分词）
items.example: The commencing phase lasts two weeks.
items.exampleCN: 起始阶段持续两周。

items.meaning: first, at the beginning
items.meaningCN: 最初的；开头的（initium“开端”+ -al）
items.example: The initial results look promising.
items.exampleCN: 最初的结果看起来不错。

items.meaning: to set a process going; to admit someone into a group
items.meaningCN: 发起；使入门（initium + -ate）
items.example: They initiated a review of the policy.
items.exampleCN: 他们启动了对这项政策的审查。

items.meaning: the act of starting, or a formal admission
items.meaningCN: 发起；入会仪式（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: The initiation of the project took a month.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目的启动花了一个月。

items.meaning: the ability to act first; a new plan
items.meaningCN: 主动性；新倡议（-ative 构成形容词或名词）
items.example: She took the initiative to call a meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她主动发起了一次会议。

items.meaning: the beginning of an institution or project
items.meaningCN: 开端；创立（in-“进入”+ capere“拿取”，同表“起始”）
items.example: The club has grown since its inception.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部自创立以来不断壮大。

definition_zh: 评论；意见；说明；注解；批评
definition_en: a spoken or written remark that gives an opinion or explanation
core_image: 在书页边缘写下一行小字，把自己的看法留在原文旁边
scene: 编辑在稿件页边拿着红笔。 The editor wrote a comment in the margin of the manuscript, reminding the author to add the source of the data.
sceneCN: 这里 comment 是「批注、说明性评论」（第 2 个义项：对文本作出的解释或意见）；句意：编辑在稿件页边写下批注，提醒作者补上数据来源。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 评论者（尤指网络评论者）

senses.title: A remark that gives an opinion
senses.definition: a spoken or written remark that states what someone thinks
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面表达某人看法的言辞
senses.example: He made a brief comment about the weather and left.
senses.exampleCN: 他随口说了句天气，就走了。
senses.why: The Latin word began as something 'devised or thought out'. A comment is a thought that has been made public, attached to whatever it is about.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词最初指“想出来、构思出来的东西”。评论就是一个被公开的想法，附着在它所谈论的对象上。

senses.title: An explanatory note on a text
senses.definition: a note that explains or clarifies a passage in a text
senses.definitionCN: 解释或阐明文中某段的注释
senses.example: The editor's comments in the margin clarified the difficult line.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑写在页边的批注把那段难懂的句子讲清楚了。
senses.why: This is the oldest written sense: a scholar's thought placed beside someone else's words, so the two can be read together.
senses.whyCN: 这是最早的书面义：学者把自己的想法放在别人的文字旁边，让两者可以并读。

senses.title: A critical remark
senses.definition: a remark that points out a fault or expresses disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 指出缺点或表示不满的言辞
senses.example: Her comment on the draft was blunt but useful.
senses.exampleCN: 她对初稿的评论很直白，但很有用。
senses.why: Once a remark is placed next to another's work, it can judge that work. The neutral 'note' turns into criticism without changing its shape.
senses.whyCN: 一句评语一旦放在别人的作品旁边，就可能变成对作品的评判。中性的“批注”不改形状，就变成了批评。

senses.title: An online response
senses.definition: a short public response posted under an article, video, or social media post
senses.definitionCN: 发布在文章、视频或社交媒体帖子下的简短公开回应
senses.example: The video drew thousands of comments overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 这个视频一夜之间引来数千条评论。
senses.why: The margin has moved: the note now sits under the post instead of beside the page. The social function is the same, a thought attached in public.
senses.whyCN: “页边”换了地方：批注现在位于帖子下方，而不是书页旁边。社会功能没有变，仍是把想法公开附着在对象上。

senses.title: A statement to the public
senses.definition: an official statement made to the press or the public
senses.definitionCN: 向媒体或公众作出的正式表态
senses.example: The police declined to comment on the case.
senses.exampleCN: 警方拒绝就此案发表评论。
senses.why: An official comment is a thought the institution chooses to release. What is withheld matters too, which is why 'no comment' became a fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 官方评论是机构选择公开的想法。被扣下的部分同样重要，所以“no comment”成了固定说法。

senses.title: A note inside computer code
senses.definition: text in a program that explains the code and is ignored by the machine
senses.definitionCN: 程序中解释代码、不被机器执行的文字
senses.example: Add a comment above the function so the next reader understands it.
senses.exampleCN: 在函数上方加一条注释，让下一个读代码的人能看懂。
senses.why: Code also has margins. A comment is written for humans only, a thought parked beside instructions that the compiler skips.
senses.whyCN: 代码也有“页边”。注释只写给人看，是停在指令旁边、被编译器跳过的一段想法。

senses.title: No comment
senses.definition: the fixed phrase used to refuse to answer a question
senses.definitionCN: 用于拒绝回答问题的固定说法
senses.example: When asked about the deal, she said only 'no comment'.
senses.exampleCN: 被问及这笔交易时，她只说了一句“无可奉告”。
senses.why: Refusing to comment is still a comment: it tells the listener that the speaker has a position but will not state it. Silence becomes a message.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝评论本身仍是一种评论：它告诉听者，说话者有立场，但不打算说出来。沉默变成了一条讯息。

senses.title: To remark or observe
senses.definition: to say something that gives your opinion about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 说出对某人或某事的看法
senses.example: Several readers commented that the ending felt rushed.
senses.exampleCN: 好几位读者评论说，结尾显得太仓促。
senses.why: The verb turns the note into an act. The thought is still placed beside its object; it is simply being placed there now.
senses.whyCN: 动词把这个“批注”变成动作。想法仍然放在对象旁边，只是“放”发生在当下。

senses.title: To annotate a text
senses.definition: to add explanatory notes to a text
senses.definitionCN: 为文本添加解释性注释
senses.example: He commented the old poem for his students.
senses.exampleCN: 他为学生给这首古诗作了注。
senses.why: Here the writer works through the text line by line, leaving a trail of thoughts beside the original. This is comment as scholarship rather than conversation.
senses.whyCN: 这里作者逐行处理文本，在原文旁留下一串想法。这是作为学术工作的 comment，而不是闲聊式的评论。

intro.en: Comment started as a word for something invented or thought up, then settled into the margin. Its path from 'devised' to 'remarked' explains why a comment can be either a note or an opinion.
intro.cn: comment 最初指“被构想出来的东西”，后来定居在书页边缘。它从“构思”走到“评论”的路径，解释了为什么 comment 既可以是注释，也可以是看法。

items.en: Comminisci meant 'to contrive, devise, invent'. It was built from com- (intensive) plus the root of mens 'mind'.
items.cn: comminisci 意为“构思、设计、发明”，由加强语气的 com- 加 mens“心智”的词根构成。

items.en: Commentum in classical Latin meant 'an invention, a fabrication'. In later Latin it shifted to 'an interpretation, a written comment'.
items.cn: commentum 在古典拉丁语中意为“发明、虚构”，到后期拉丁语转为“解释、书面评注”。

items.en: English borrowed comment in the 14th century with the sense 'an explanatory note'. It belonged first to scholars and law, not to daily conversation.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪借入 comment，意为“解释性注释”。它最初属于学者与法律文书，而不是日常谈话。

items.en: The sense widened from a note on a text to any remark expressing an opinion. The verb followed the noun.
items.cn: 词义从“文本注释”扩大到“任何表达看法的言辞”，动词随后出现。

items.en: Comment gained new homes: press statements, online threads, and programming. 'No comment' became a standard refusal, and code comments became part of software writing.
items.cn: comment 又获得新的栖身之处：新闻表态、网络帖子与编程。“no comment”成为标准拒绝语，代码注释也成为软件写作的一部分。

items.en: The root men- 'to think' also underlies mental, mention and mentor, though the exact reconstruction of the family is debated, so the deepest step is source uncertain.
items.cn: 词根 men-“思考”也支撑着 mental、mention、mentor，但该词族的确切重构存在争议，故最深层来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to begin formally. It shares the comm- opening and a similar ending but means starting, not remarking.
entries.definitionCN: 正式开始。同样以 comm- 开头、结尾相近，但意思是“开始”，不是“评论”。

entries.definition: to praise or recommend. It sounds close but carries approval rather than observation.
entries.definitionCN: 称赞；推荐。读音接近，但传达的是赞许，而不是观察。

entries.definition: a series of comments, or a running description of an event. It is built directly on comment.
entries.definitionCN: 系列评论；评注；现场解说。它直接由 comment 构成。

entries.definition: a small community sharing resources. It shares the comm- start but has nothing to do with remarks.
entries.definitionCN: 公社；共同生活的小群体。同样以 comm- 开头，但与“评论”无关。

entries.definition: something said casually as an observation. It is lighter and more conversational than comment.
entries.definitionCN: 谈论；言论。比 comment 更轻、更口语化，常指随口说出的话。

entries.definition: a statement based on something noticed. It stresses what was seen rather than the opinion held.
entries.definitionCN: 观察所得的意见。强调“看到了什么”，而不是“持什么立场”。

entries.definition: a short written record or explanation. It matches the margin sense of comment.
entries.definitionCN: 笔记；注释。对应 comment 的“页边批注”义。

entries.definition: the act of judging faults, or a detailed analysis of a work. It is stronger and more evaluative than comment.
entries.definitionCN: 批评；评论文章。比 comment 更强、更具评价性。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: the Latin comminisci 'devise', the shared men- root of mental and mention, and the places where English actually writes comments.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 comminisci“构思”、与 mental、mention 共享的 men- 词根，以及英语实际写 comment 的场所。

normal.en: comment and mental share the men- root: a comment is a thought (mens) put into words.
normal.cn: comment 与 mental 共享 men- 词根：评论就是把心里的想法（mens）写成话。

normal.en: The original commentum was 'something devised'. A comment is a devised thought attached to its subject.
normal.cn: 最初的 commentum 是“构想出来的东西”。评论就是被构想出来、再附着到对象上的想法。

normal.en: A code comment is written for the next human, not for the compiler: the margin moved into the source file.
normal.cn: 代码注释是写给下一个人类看的，不是给编译器看的：页边搬进了源文件。

normal.en: Commentary runs alongside an event the way margin notes run alongside a page.
normal.cn: commentary 伴随事件进行，就像页边批注伴随书页存在。

normal.en: No comment is still a message: the refusal tells you a position exists but stays unspoken.
normal.cn: no comment 仍是一条讯息：拒绝本身告诉你“有立场，但不说”。

abstract.en: The core picture is a second layer of writing: the original text stays, and a lighter hand writes beside it.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是第二层书写：原文不动，另一只手在它旁边写下更轻的字。

abstract.en: The margin keeps moving: page edge, press briefing, comment thread, source code. The relation between text and note stays the same.
abstract.cn: “页边”不断移动：书页边缘、新闻发布、评论串、源代码。文本与批注之间的关系始终未变。

abstract.en: So comment is never quite independent: it always leans on something else that it explains, judges, or answers.
abstract.cn: 所以 comment 从不完全独立：它总要倚靠某个被它解释、评判或回应的东西。

examples.en: The teacher wrote a short comment at the end of each essay.
examples.cn: 老师在每篇作文末尾写了一句简短的评语。

examples.en: He refused to comment on the rumours.
examples.cn: 他拒绝就那些传闻发表评论。

examples.en: Please read the comments in the code before changing the settings.
examples.cn: 修改设置前，请先读代码里的注释。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠门谈」——靠在门边小声谈，一句句都是评论 → comment 评论

root: 源自拉丁语 comminisci“构思、想出”，名词 commentum 由“发明、虚构”转为“解释、评注”，核心是“把想法写在对象旁边”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of comment, all built on a thought placed beside something else: a margin note, an explanation, a criticism, a public statement, a social media reply, a line of code, a refusal to speak, and the acts of remarking and annotating.
sensesIntro.cn: comment 的九个义项都建立在“把想法放到某物旁边”上：页边批注、解释、批评、公开表态、网络回复、一行代码、拒绝发言，以及“评论”和“作注”这两个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second layer of writing placed beside an original text.
core.cn: 核心意象：在原文旁边写下的第二层文字。

branches.en: A THOUGHT SPOKEN: an opinion offered aloud is the margin note turned into talk.
branches.cn: 说出的想法：口头给出的看法，就是变成话语的页边批注。

branches.en: A THOUGHT EXPLAINING: a note clarifies a passage, and annotating is the act of writing that trail of notes.
branches.cn: 解释性的想法：注释阐明某段文字，作注则是把这一串注释写下来的动作。

branches.en: A THOUGHT JUDGING: the note beside a work can point out its faults.
branches.cn: 评判性的想法：作品旁边的批注可以指出它的缺点。

branches.en: A THOUGHT PUBLISHED: threads under a post and statements to the press are public margins.
branches.cn: 公开的想法：帖子下的评论串和面向媒体的表态，都是公共的“页边”。

branches.en: WRITTEN FOR MACHINES OR WITHHELD: a code comment is skipped by the machine, and no comment is a message left deliberately blank.
branches.cn: 写给机器或有意留白：代码注释被机器跳过，no comment 则是故意留空的一条讯息。

intro.en: Comment is a Latin noun that English borrowed whole. Its -ment is not an English suffix here but part of the Latin participle; English later adds -ary, -ator, -ate and -er to build the family.
intro.cn: comment 是英语整体借入的拉丁名词。这里的 -ment 不是英语后缀，而是拉丁分词的一部分；英语后来加 -ary、-ator、-ate、-er 来扩展词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is comminisci 'to devise', with the mind-root men- (mens 'mind'). English relatives through meaning include mental, mention and mentor; the comment- family itself runs through commentary and commentator.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基干是 comminisci“构思”，含表“心智”的词根 men-（mens“心”）。意义上相关的英语词有 mental、mention、mentor；comment 本身这一族则由 commentary 与 commentator 延续。

items.meaning: a devised thought; a note or remark
items.meaningCN: 评论；注释（com- 表加强，men- 表“心智”）
items.example: Her comment was short and fair.
items.exampleCN: 她的评论简短而公允。

items.meaning: a set of comments; a running explanation
items.meaningCN: 评论集；评注；现场解说（-ary 表示集合或事物）
items.example: The book includes a commentary on each poem.
items.exampleCN: 这本书为每首诗配有评注。

items.meaning: one who comments, especially on events or sport
items.meaningCN: 评论员；解说员（-or 表示做动作的人）
items.example: The commentator described the final lap.
items.exampleCN: 解说员描述了最后一圈。

items.meaning: to provide a running commentary
items.meaningCN: 作现场解说；作评注（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: She commentated on the match for radio.
items.exampleCN: 她为电台解说这场比赛。

items.meaning: a person who leaves a comment, especially online
items.meaningCN: 评论者（尤指网络评论者，-er 表示人）
items.example: One commenter corrected the date.
items.exampleCN: 一位评论者纠正了日期。

items.meaning: relating to commentary or annotation
items.meaningCN: 评注性的；注释的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The commentarial tradition is centuries old.
items.exampleCN: 这一评注传统已有数百年历史。

items.meaning: relating to the mind
items.meaningCN: 心理的；精神的（同 men- 词根 + -al）
items.example: The work demands mental stamina.
items.exampleCN: 这项工作需要脑力耐力。

items.meaning: to refer to something briefly
items.meaningCN: 提及；说起（同一“心智”词族的拉丁名词）
items.example: She mentioned the deadline twice.
items.exampleCN: 她两次提到截止日期。

items.meaning: an experienced adviser
items.meaningCN: 导师；顾问（常被与“心智”词族联想，但词源另有来源）
items.example: He acted as mentor to the new staff.
items.exampleCN: 他担任新员工的导师。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 虚构之物；后指解释、评注

latinEntries.meaning: a mentioning, a calling to mind

definition_zh: 商业的；以营利为目的的；商业化的；广告（片）
definition_en: relating to buying and selling, or intended to make a profit
core_image: 柜台两侧一手交钱一手交货，货物挂着价签流动
scene: 晚间节目中途，电视屏幕切进一段汽车画面。 During the evening programme a car commercial ran for thirty seconds before the news came back.
sceneCN: 这里 commercial 是「广告片」（第 4 个义项：电视或广播中的广告）；句意：晚间节目里插播了一段三十秒的汽车广告，随后画面切回新闻。

pos.zh: 商业的；商业性的；以营利为目的的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 非商业性的；不以营利为目的的

senses.title: Relating to trade
senses.definition: connected with the buying and selling of goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 与商品和服务的买卖有关的
senses.example: The city is a major commercial centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市是重要的商业中心。
senses.why: The Latin base is commercium, 'trade together', from merx 'merchandise'. Commercial simply means 'belonging to that exchange'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语基干是 commercium“共同交易”，来自 merx“商品”。commercial 就是“属于这种交换的”。

senses.title: Run for profit
senses.definition: organized or operated with the aim of making money
senses.definitionCN: 以赚钱为目的来组织或运营的
senses.example: It began as a hobby and became a commercial venture.
senses.exampleCN: 它起初是爱好，后来变成了营利事业。
senses.why: Trade has a purpose: money. When an activity is called commercial, the question 'who profits?' has already been answered.
senses.whyCN: 交易有目的：钱。当一项活动被称为 commercial，就意味着“谁获利”这个问题已经答完了。

senses.title: Successful in the market
senses.definition: popular or profitable enough to succeed as a product
senses.definitionCN: 足够受欢迎或赚钱、作为产品取得成功
senses.example: The film was a commercial success but a critical failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影票房成功，评论却一败涂地。
senses.why: This sense measures success in sales rather than in art. The same adjective that names the field also names the score.
senses.whyCN: 这一义用销量而不是艺术水准来衡量成功。同一个形容词既命名领域，也命名比分。

senses.title: An advertisement
senses.definition: a short advertisement on television, radio, or online
senses.definitionCN: 电视、广播或网络上的短广告
senses.example: The commercial lasted thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这则广告持续三十秒。
senses.why: Broadcast advertising is the most concentrated form of commerce: a paid slot whose only job is to sell. English turned the adjective into a noun for that slot.
senses.whyCN: 广播广告是商业最浓缩的形态：一段付费时段，唯一任务就是卖东西。英语把形容词直接变成了指这段时段的名词。

senses.title: Made to sell rather than to express
senses.definition: designed to appeal to a mass market, often at the cost of artistic quality
senses.definitionCN: 为迎合大众市场而设计，常牺牲艺术品质
senses.example: The album felt too commercial for his early fans.
senses.exampleCN: 老歌迷觉得这张专辑太商业化了。
senses.why: The adjective can be a criticism: when profit shapes the work, something else is bent to fit the market.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可以是一种批评：当利润塑造作品时，别的东西就被弯折去迎合市场。

senses.title: Funded by advertising
senses.definition: of broadcasting, financed by advertisements rather than by the state or subscribers
senses.definitionCN: （广播）靠广告而非国家或订户资助运营的
senses.example: Commercial television changed the evening schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 商业电视改变了晚间节目安排。
senses.why: The money comes from advertisers, so the audience is the product being sold. The adjective marks that funding model.
senses.whyCN: 钱来自广告主，于是观众成了被出售的“产品”。这个形容词标记的正是这种资金来源。

senses.title: Business law and affairs
senses.definition: relating to business transactions and the law governing them
senses.definitionCN: 与商业交易及规范它的法律有关的
senses.example: The dispute went to commercial court.
senses.exampleCN: 这场纠纷交由商事法庭审理。
senses.why: Law separates deals between firms from deals between private persons. Commercial is the label on the firm-to-firm side.
senses.whyCN: 法律把公司间的交易与私人间的交易分开。commercial 就是贴在“公司对公司”这一侧的标签。

senses.title: Commercial vehicles
senses.definition: of vehicles, built for carrying goods or paying passengers rather than private use
senses.definitionCN: （车辆）为运货或载客收费而造，而非私人使用
senses.example: Only commercial traffic may use this lane.
senses.exampleCN: 这条车道只允许商用车辆通行。
senses.why: A van earns money while a family car costs money. The same adjective sorts vehicles by whether they are working.
senses.whyCN: 货车在赚钱，家用车在花钱。同一个形容词按“是否在干活”把车辆分了类。

intro.en: Commercial is the adjective of commerce, built on Latin merx 'merchandise'. Its advertising noun is a 20th-century shortening of 'commercial advertisement'.
intro.cn: commercial 是 commerce 的形容词，建立在拉丁语 merx“商品”上。它的“广告”名词义，是 20 世纪对 commercial advertisement 的缩略。

items.en: Commercium meant 'trade, traffic, commerce', from com- 'together' plus merx (genitive mercis) 'merchandise'.
items.cn: commercium 意为“贸易、往来、商业”，由 com-“一起”加 merx（属格 mercis）“商品”构成。

items.en: Merc- also gives mercari 'to trade', mercatus 'market', and mercator 'trader'. English merchant, merchandise, market and mercantile descend from these.
items.cn: merc- 还给出 mercari“交易”、mercatus“市场”、mercator“商人”。英语的 merchant、merchandise、market、mercantile 都由此而来。

items.en: Commerce entered English in the 16th century from French. The adjective commercial appears in the 17th century, first in the phrase 'commercial affairs'.
items.cn: commerce 于 16 世纪经法语进入英语。形容词 commercial 出现于 17 世纪，最早见于“商业事务”这类说法。

items.en: Commercial expanded into law, transport and banking: commercial law, commercial vehicle, commercial bank. The adjective became a general classifier for anything money-making.
items.cn: commercial 在 19 世纪扩及法律、运输与银行：商法、商用车辆、商业银行。这个形容词成了任何“赚钱之事”的通用分类标签。

items.en: Commercial as a noun for a broadcast advertisement is a 20th-century shortening. Commercial television and the commercial break grew with broadcasting economics.
items.cn: 名词义“广播广告”是 20 世纪的缩略说法；商业电视与广告时段随广播经济一同成长。

items.en: The root of merx is not securely established; it may be connected to merces 'wages, price'. The deepest link is therefore source uncertain.
items.cn: merx 的词根并未可靠确定，可能与 merces“报酬、价格”有关。因此最深层联系来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the activity of buying and selling. It is the noun that commercial describes.
entries.definitionCN: 商业；贸易。它就是 commercial 所修饰的那个名词。

entries.definition: to make something commercial or profit-oriented. It is built on commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 使商业化。它由 commercial 构成。

entries.definition: to begin formally. It shares the opening com- but not the merc- root.
entries.definitionCN: 正式开始。同样以 com- 开头，但没有 merc- 词根。

entries.definition: a product that can be traded. It comes from a different root (modus 'measure'), not from merx.
entries.definitionCN: 商品；大宗物资。词根不同（modus“尺度”），并非来自 merx。

entries.definition: relating to trade and merchants. It is the older, more bookish adjective from the same merc- root.
entries.definitionCN: 商业的；商人的。同出 merc- 词根，但更古老、更书面。

entries.definition: commercial activity, or a company. The everyday word, wider than commercial and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 商业；公司。最日常的词，范围比 commercial 更宽，也不那么技术化。

entries.definition: producing money as a result. It names the outcome rather than the field.
entries.definitionCN: 有利可图的。说的是结果，而不是所属领域。

entries.definition: a public notice promoting a product. Commercial is the broadcast shortening of it.
entries.definitionCN: 广告。commercial 是它在广播语境中的缩略说法。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin merx 'merchandise', the English merchant and market family, and the fixed phrases commercial break and commercial vehicle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 merx“商品”、英语 merchant 与 market 词族，以及 commercial break、commercial vehicle 等固定搭配。

normal.en: commercial and merchant share merc-: both are about moving merchandise.
normal.cn: commercial 与 merchant 共享 merc-：两者都关于商品流转。

normal.en: market comes from Latin mercatus, so the marketplace is the concrete home of the commercial.
normal.cn: market 来自拉丁语 mercatus，市场就是“商业”的具体家园。

normal.en: A commercial break is where the programme stops and the selling starts.
normal.cn: commercial break 是节目停下、销售开始的地方。

normal.en: Commercial success is measured in money; critical success is measured in judgment. The pair of phrases keeps the two scores apart.
normal.cn: commercial success 用钱衡量，critical success 用评价衡量；这两个搭配把两套比分分开。

normal.en: Commercial television is paid for by advertisers, so the adjective also names a funding model.
normal.cn: 商业电视由广告主付费，所以这个形容词也在命名一种资金来源。

abstract.en: The core picture is a counter with a price tag: every sense of commercial involves something being valued for what it can fetch.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是挂着价签的柜台：commercial 的每个义项都涉及“按能卖多少钱来估值”。

abstract.en: The word spreads from the market to law, transport, broadcasting and art, carrying the same question: is money the point?
abstract.cn: 这个词从市场扩散到法律、运输、广播与艺术，携带的始终是同一个问题：钱是不是目的？

abstract.en: When the adjective becomes a noun, the whole activity shrinks to one paid slot of time.
abstract.cn: 当形容词变成名词，整项活动就缩成了一段付费的时间。

examples.en: The harbour handles both commercial and passenger traffic.
examples.cn: 这个港口同时处理商业货运与客运。

examples.en: The play was praised by critics but never a commercial success.
examples.cn: 这部戏受到评论界称赞，却从未在商业上成功。

examples.en: He switched off during the commercial break.
examples.cn: 广告时段一到，他就关掉了电视。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可摸手」——柜台上一手交钱一手交货，可摸得着的手就是生意 → commercial 商业的

root: 源自拉丁语 commercium“贸易”，由 com-“一起”+ merx（属格 mercis）“商品”构成，核心是“围绕商品的交换”，故兼有“商业的”与“营利性”之义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of commercial, all circling the price tag: trade itself, profit as the aim, market success, the broadcast advertisement, art bent to the market, advertising-funded media, business law, and revenue-earning vehicles.
sensesIntro.cn: commercial 的八个义项都绕着价签转：贸易本身、以营利为目的、市场成功、广播广告、向市场弯折的艺术、靠广告运营的媒体、商事法律，以及用来赚钱的车辆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a counter with a price tag, where things are exchanged for money.
core.cn: 核心意象：挂着价签的柜台，东西在这里换成钱。

branches.en: THE FIELD: trade itself, the law that governs it, and the vehicles that carry it are all labelled by the same adjective.
branches.cn: 领域：贸易本身、规范它的法律、承载它的车辆，都由同一个形容词标注。

branches.en: THE PURPOSE: profit is the aim, and the adjective describes whatever is run for it.
branches.cn: 目的：利润是目标，这个形容词描述为此而运作的事物。

branches.en: THE MEDIA SLOT: an advertisement fills a paid break, and commercial broadcasting lives on those payments.
branches.cn: 媒体时段：广告填满付费时段，商业广播就靠这些付费生存。

branches.en: THE CRITICISM: when selling shapes the work, commercial becomes a negative word for art.
branches.cn: 批评义：当销售塑造作品时，commercial 成了评价艺术时的贬义词。

branches.en: MARKET SUCCESS: the measured score, the hit that sells.
branches.cn: 市场成功：被量出来的成绩，卖得动的热门产品。

intro.en: Commercial is commerce plus the Latin adjective ending -al. English then adds -ize, -ization, -ly and -ism, all still transparent.
intro.cn: commercial 是 commerce 加拉丁形容词后缀 -al。英语随后又加 -ize、-ization、-ly、-ism，这些后缀至今仍然透明。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base merx 'merchandise' is more productive than the modern word suggests: mercari, mercatus and mercator give English merchant, market, mercantile and merchandise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基干 merx“商品”的能产性比现代词面看上去更强：mercari、mercatus、mercator 给出英语的 merchant、market、mercantile、merchandise。

items.meaning: the exchange of goods and services
items.meaningCN: 商业；贸易（com- 表“一起”，merx 表“商品”）
items.example: Commerce between the two ports grew.
items.exampleCN: 两个港口之间的贸易增长了。

items.meaning: relating to trade or profit
items.meaningCN: 商业的；营利的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The area is zoned for commercial use.
items.exampleCN: 这片区域被划为商业用途。

items.meaning: to make something a matter of commerce
items.meaningCN: 使商业化（-ize 表“使成为”）
items.example: They commercialized the traditional festival.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这个传统节日商业化了。

items.meaning: the process of making something commercial
items.meaningCN: 商业化（-ation 构成动作名词）
items.example: The commercialization of sport worries fans.
items.exampleCN: 体育的商业化让球迷担忧。

items.meaning: in commercial terms; from a business point of view
items.meaningCN: 商业上；从商业角度看（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The process is not commercially viable yet.
items.exampleCN: 这个工艺目前在商业上还不可行。

items.meaning: excessive emphasis on profit
items.meaningCN: 商业主义；唯利是图（-ism 表示主义或态度）
items.example: Critics blamed commercialism for the change.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把这一变化归咎于商业主义。

items.structure: Old French marchant, from Latin mercari (to trade)
items.meaning: a person who buys and sells goods
items.meaningCN: 商人（同 merc- 词根，经法语进入英语）
items.example: A merchant sold silk at the fair.
items.exampleCN: 一位商人在集市上卖丝绸。

items.meaning: goods for sale
items.meaningCN: 商品；货物（同一 merc- 词族）
items.example: The shop displays its merchandise outside.
items.exampleCN: 这家店把商品摆在门外。

items.meaning: a place or system of buying and selling
items.meaningCN: 市场（拉丁 mercatus“交易、市场”）
items.example: The market opens at six.
items.exampleCN: 市场六点开门。

items.meaning: connected with trade and merchants
items.meaningCN: 商业的；商人的（-ile 构成形容词）
items.example: The town had a strong mercantile class.
items.exampleCN: 这座城镇有一个强大的商人阶层。

definition_zh: 委托；委员会；佣金；任命；委任状；（使）服役
definition_en: an official task or authority given to someone, or the group or payment that comes with it
core_image: 把一件任务写进委任状，交到受托人手里
scene: 画廊大厅里，老板和年轻画家对着壁画草稿。 The gallery owner gave a young painter a commission to paint a three-metre mural for the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 commission 是「委托创作」（第 4 个义项：付费委托艺术家完成作品）；句意：画廊老板委托一位年轻画家为大厅画一幅三米宽的壁画。

pos.zh: 委托；委员会；佣金；任命；委任状
委托；任命；使（设备）投入使用

senses.title: A task entrusted to someone
senses.definition: an official instruction or authority to carry out a task
senses.definitionCN: 要求某人执行某项任务的正式指示或授权
senses.example: The council gave the engineer a commission to survey the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 市议会委托这位工程师勘测这座桥。
senses.why: The Latin noun is 'a committing'. Something is handed over to another person, who now has the authority to act on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词意为“一次交托”。某件事被交到另一个人手里，此人从此有权去办它。

senses.title: A body appointed to investigate
senses.definition: a group of people officially appointed to examine a matter
senses.definitionCN: 被正式任命审查某事的群体
senses.example: A commission was set up to investigate the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 成立了一个委员会来调查这起事故。
senses.why: When one person's entrusted task becomes too large, it is given to several. The body takes the name of the charge it holds.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人的受托任务太大，就交给几个人。这个机构便继承了它所承担之事的名字。

senses.title: A percentage paid to an agent
senses.definition: a sum paid to a salesperson or agent, usually a share of the sale
senses.definitionCN: 付给销售员或代理人的款项，通常是成交额的一部分
senses.example: She earns a five per cent commission on every sale.
senses.exampleCN: 每笔销售她抽取百分之五的佣金。
senses.why: The agent acts on a commission, a task entrusted by the seller. Payment follows the completed charge, so the task and its reward share one word.
senses.whyCN: 代理人按“委托”行事，任务是卖方交托的。报酬在任务完成后支付，于是任务与报酬共用同一个词。

senses.title: An order for a work of art
senses.definition: a formal request to an artist to create a particular work, or the work so created
senses.definitionCN: 正式请艺术家创作某件作品，也指由此完成的作品
senses.example: The museum commissioned a new portrait of the founder.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆委托创作一幅创始人的新肖像。
senses.why: Patronage is a commission in the literal sense: the patron entrusts a work to the artist and pays for it. The noun can name either the order or the finished piece.
senses.whyCN: 赞助就是字面意义上的 commission：赞助人把一件作品交托给艺术家并付钱。名词既可指委托，也可指完成之作。

senses.title: An officer's appointment
senses.definition: the official rank and authority of a military officer
senses.definitionCN: 军官的正式军衔与指挥权
senses.example: He received his commission as a lieutenant.
senses.exampleCN: 他获得了中尉的委任。
senses.why: A military commission is authority handed down from the state to one person. The document and the rank keep the same name.
senses.whyCN: 军官委任是国家把指挥权交到一个人手里。委任状与军衔都沿用同一个名字。

senses.title: The committing of a crime
senses.definition: the act of committing a crime or offence, in the fixed phrase 'commission of an offence'
senses.definitionCN: 实施犯罪或违法行为，用于固定说法 commission of an offence
senses.example: The report documented the commission of several offences.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了数起违法犯罪行为的发生。
senses.why: This is the dark twin of entrusted work: instead of doing what was asked, one does what is forbidden. English borrowed the same noun for the doing itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是“受托任务”的阴暗孪生：不是去做被要求的事，而是去做被禁止的事。英语用同一个名词指这项行为本身。

senses.title: In or out of commission
senses.titleCN: 处于可用或不可用状态
senses.definition: the state of a ship or machine being in service, or out of service when damaged
senses.definitionCN: 船只或机器处于服役可用状态，或损坏停用时表示不可用
senses.example: The ferry is out of commission for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘渡轮正在维修，暂停使用。
senses.why: A working ship is 'in commission', holding the authority to operate. Damage revokes that authority, so the machine is literally out of its charge.
senses.whyCN: 在役的船处于 in commission，持有“可以运作”的授权。损坏撤销了这份授权，于是机器字面上“出了职守”。

senses.title: To appoint or authorize
senses.definition: to give someone official authority to act, especially in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 正式授予某人行动权，尤用于军队
senses.example: The president commissioned him as an adviser.
senses.exampleCN: 总统任命他为顾问。
senses.why: The verb is the act that creates the noun: authority is handed over, and the person now carries a commission.
senses.whyCN: 动词是造出名词的那个动作：授权被交出去，此人从此带着一份委任。

senses.title: Put a system into service
senses.titleCN: 使设备或系统投入使用
senses.definition: to prepare and start a new machine, building, or system so that it can operate
senses.definitionCN: 调试并启动新机器、建筑或系统，使其可运行
senses.example: The plant was commissioned in March.
senses.exampleCN: 这座工厂于三月投入运行。
senses.why: An engineer 'commissions' a plant by formally handing it over to operation. The sense extends the military idea of entering service to machines.
senses.whyCN: 工程师对工厂进行 commissioning，就是把它正式交给运营。这一义把军事上的“进入服役”扩展到机器。

intro.en: Commission is the noun made from Latin committere, the same verb that gives English commit. The two words are a doublet: one arrived as a verb, the other as a noun.
intro.cn: commission 是由拉丁语 committere 构成的名词，而同一个动词也给出了英语 commit。二者是一对“双式词”：一个以动词身份进来，一个以名词身份进来。

items.en: Committere meant 'to unite, connect; entrust, commit; do, perpetrate'. It was built from com- 'with' plus mittere 'to send'.
items.cn: committere 意为“连接、联合；托付、交办；做出、实施”，由 com-“一起”加 mittere“送出”构成。

items.en: Commissio, the noun of action, meant 'a committing or entrusting'. It could name both the handing over of a task and the delegation of authority.
items.cn: 动作名词 commissio 意为“交托、委任”，既可指任务的交付，也可指权力的授予。

items.en: English borrowed commission through Old French around 1300 with the sense 'authority entrusted'. The verb commit entered separately from the same Latin verb.
items.cn: 英语约在 1300 年经古法语借入 commission，意为“被授予的权力”。动词 commit 则由同一个拉丁动词另行进入英语。

items.en: The sense 'a body of persons appointed with authority' appears by the mid-15th century. This is the ancestor of modern commissions of inquiry.
items.cn: “受权任命的一群人”这一义在 15 世纪中期出现，是现代“调查委员会”的祖先。

items.en: The financial sense 'fee paid to an agent' is recorded in the 18th century, when agency work was paid by a share of the transaction.
items.cn: “付给代理人的佣金”这一财政义记录于 18 世纪，当时代理工作按交易分成取酬。

items.en: Modern English keeps the whole cluster: task, body, fee, art order, officer's rank, crime, service state, and the verb 'put into service'. The unifying idea is still something handed over.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了整簇义项：任务、机构、佣金、艺术委托、军官衔、犯罪、服役状态，以及动词“投入使用”。统一的意思仍是“被交托出去的东西”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to carry out, entrust, or pledge. It comes from the same Latin verb as commission, but entered English as a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 犯（罪）；托付；承诺。它与 commission 同出一个拉丁动词，但以动词身份进入英语。

entries.definition: a promise or dedication. It is the noun from commit, not from commission.
entries.definitionCN: 承诺；投入。它是 commit 的名词，而不是 commission 的。

entries.definition: a group appointed to deal with a matter. It is historically the same 'entrusted body' idea, borrowed through a different route.
entries.definitionCN: 委员会。历史上是同一个“受托群体”概念，只是经由不同路径借入。

entries.definition: a member of a commission or a senior official. It is built directly on commission.
entries.definitionCN: 委员；专员；部门主管。它直接由 commission 构成。

entries.definition: a group chosen to make decisions or manage affairs. It is the everyday word for a standing body, while commission often implies a specific charge.
entries.definitionCN: 委员会。日常用词，多为常设机构；commission 则常带一项具体任务。

entries.definition: official authority to act, given by voters or a higher body. It stresses the source of authority.
entries.definitionCN: 授权；委托。强调权力的来源。

entries.definition: money paid for a service. It matches the commission sense of payment, but without the share-of-sale idea.
entries.definitionCN: 服务费。对应佣金义，但不含“按成交分成”的意思。

entries.definition: a request for goods or a piece of work. It overlaps with commissioning art or equipment.
entries.definitionCN: 订单；委托。与“委托创作或订制设备”义重叠。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin committere, the English doublet commit, and the fixed phrases on commission and out of commission.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 committere、英语双式词 commit，以及 on commission、out of commission 等固定搭配。

normal.en: commission and commit are twins from committere: the verb names the act, the noun names what was handed over.
normal.cn: commission 与 commit 是 committere 的双生子：动词指动作，名词指被交托的东西。

normal.en: com- 'together' + mittere 'send': a commission is something sent into another person's hands.
normal.cn: com-“一起”+ mittere“送出”：commission 就是被送到别人手里的一件事。

normal.en: A salesperson on commission is paid when the entrusted task is completed.
normal.cn: 拿佣金的销售员，在受托任务完成时才拿到钱。

normal.en: An officer's commission is a piece of paper and a rank: both are authority sent down from the state.
normal.cn: 军官的 commission 既是一张纸也是一个军衔：两者都是国家向下送出的权力。

normal.en: Out of commission means the machine's authority to run has been withdrawn, so it sits idle.
normal.cn: out of commission 指机器的“运行授权”被撤回，只能闲置。

abstract.en: The core picture is a sealed envelope changing hands: the task leaves the giver and enters the agent.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一封换手的密封信：任务离开委托者，进入受托者。

abstract.en: All senses keep that transfer: authority, a body, a fee, a painting, a rank, a crime, a machine's service status.
abstract.cn: 所有义项都保留这次转移：权力、机构、佣金、画作、军衔、罪行、机器的服役状态。

abstract.en: Payment is the shadow of the charge: whoever receives the task also receives a share.
abstract.cn: 报酬是任务的影子：接下任务的人，也接下一份分成。

examples.en: The government commissioned an independent review of the system.
examples.cn: 政府委托对该系统进行独立审查。

examples.en: He works on commission, so busy months pay better.
examples.cn: 他靠佣金工作，所以忙的月份收入更高。

examples.en: The old pump is out of commission until the part arrives.
examples.cn: 旧水泵要等零件到货才能重新使用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可米神」——把米交给神，就是托付一件事，办成了再分一份 → commission 委托、佣金

root: 源自拉丁语 commissio“交托、委任”，出自 committere（com-“一起”+ mittere“送出”），与 commit 同源，核心是“把事情或权力交到别人手里”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of commission, all versions of one transfer: a task, an investigating body, an agent's fee, an art order, an officer's rank, a crime, a ship's service state, an appointment, and a plant put into operation.
sensesIntro.cn: commission 的九个义项都是同一次“交托”的变体：任务、调查机构、代理佣金、艺术委托、军官任命、罪行、船只服役状态、授权行为，以及让工厂投入运行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a task written on a document and placed into another person's hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：一项任务被写在文件上，交到另一个人手里。

branches.en: THE TRANSFER: a task is entrusted, and the verb names the act of appointing someone to it.
branches.cn: 交托本身：任务被托付，动词则指任命某人承担它的动作。

branches.en: MANY HANDS: one charge grows into a body of people appointed to investigate.
branches.cn: 多只手：一项职责长大成一群受命调查的人。

branches.en: THE PRICE OF THE CHARGE: an agent takes a share of the sale, and a patron pays for a commissioned work.
branches.cn: 任务的价钱：代理人抽取成交分成，赞助人为委托作品付费。

branches.en: ENTERING SERVICE: an officer's rank, a ship's active state, and a new plant all begin when authority to operate is granted.
branches.cn: 进入服役：军官衔、船只的现役状态、新工厂，都在“运行授权”获批时开始。

branches.en: THE DARK DOUBLE: the same noun for entrusting also names the doing of a forbidden act.
branches.cn: 阴暗的双生：同一个表示“交托”的名词，也指实施被禁止的行为。

intro.en: Commission is a Latin noun of action from committere. Its -ion is the Latin action ending; English builds commissioner, commissioned and commissionaire from it, while commit and mission belong to the same mittere family.
intro.cn: commission 是 committere 的拉丁动作名词，-ion 是拉丁动作后缀；英语由此构成 commissioner、commissioned、commissionaire，而 commit 与 mission 属于同一个 mittere 词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb mittere 'to send' is one of the most productive in English: mission, missile, transmit, submit, permit, admit, emit, remit and commit all descend from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 mittere“送出”是英语中能产性最强的词根之一：mission、missile、transmit、submit、permit、admit、emit、remit、commit 都出自它。

items.meaning: a task or authority handed over
items.meaningCN: 委托；委员会；佣金（com- 表“一起”，mittere 表“送出”）
items.example: They accepted the commission to design the hall.
items.exampleCN: 他们接下了设计大厅的委托。

items.meaning: a member of a commission; a senior official
items.meaningCN: 委员；专员（-er 表示人）
items.example: The commissioner opened the inquiry.
items.exampleCN: 专员宣布调查开始。

items.meaning: entrusted with a task; holding an officer's rank
items.meaningCN: 受委托的；已委任的（-ed 构成分词或形容词）
items.example: The commissioned study took six months.
items.exampleCN: 这项受委托的研究花了六个月。

items.meaning: a uniformed attendant or doorkeeper
items.meaningCN: （英）门卫；传达员（-aire 经法语表示人）
items.example: The commissionaire called a taxi for us.
items.exampleCN: 门卫帮我们叫了出租车。

items.meaning: to entrust, pledge, or perpetrate
items.meaningCN: 托付；承诺；犯（罪）（同一拉丁动词的英语双式词）
items.example: They committed the funds to the project.
items.exampleCN: 他们把资金投入了这个项目。

items.meaning: a pledge or dedication
items.meaningCN: 承诺；投入（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The job needs a long-term commitment.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作需要长期投入。

items.meaning: a sending out, or the task one is sent to do
items.meaningCN: 使命；任务；派出（同一 mittere 词根）
items.example: The team's mission was to map the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队的任务是测绘山谷。

items.meaning: to send across
items.meaningCN: 传送；传播（trans-“穿过”+ mittere“送出”）
items.example: The device transmits data every minute.
items.exampleCN: 这个设备每分钟传送一次数据。

items.meaning: to send in, yield
items.meaningCN: 提交；屈服（sub-“向下”+ mittere“送出”）
items.example: Please submit the form by Friday.
items.exampleCN: 请在周五前提交表格。

items.meaning: to allow to pass
items.meaningCN: 允许；许可（per-“穿过”+ mittere“送出”）
items.example: The rules permit two guests per room.
items.exampleCN: 规定允许每间房住两位客人。

definition_zh: 承诺；投入；托付；犯（罪）；收押；提交（代码）
definition_en: to promise or devote yourself to something, to entrust something, or to carry out an act
core_image: 把自己的一只手按在契约上，从此不再收回
scene: 开发者在显示器前敲完今天的最后一批代码。 The developer committed the last batch of code and wrote a message describing the change.
