sceneCN: 这里 commit 是「提交（代码变更）」（第 7 个义项：把改动永久记入版本库）；句意：开发者提交了今天的最后一批代码，并写下了说明这次改动的信息。

pos.zh: 承诺；投入；托付；犯（罪）；收押；提交

collocations.zh: 承诺做某事；投身于某事

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 坚定的；忠于某事的；已投入的
收押；交付（审判）；（葬礼）下葬
提交者（尤指代码提交者）
委托；委员会；佣金（与 commit 同出拉丁 committere）

senses.title: Pledge yourself to something
senses.definition: to promise to do something or to stay with a plan, person, or cause
senses.definitionCN: 承诺做某事，或坚持某项计划、某个人、某个事业
senses.example: The team committed to finishing the report by Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 团队承诺在周五前完成报告。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to send together with'. To commit is to send your own future action into a promise, so that it is no longer free to go elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是“一同送出”。commit 就是把自己的未来行动送进一个承诺里，使它不能再随意去别处。

senses.title: Devote money, time, or people
senses.definition: to give resources, time, or effort to a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把资源、时间或精力投入某个目标
senses.example: The company committed two million dollars to the research.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这项研究投入了两百万美元。
senses.why: A pledge becomes concrete when something valuable is handed over. Money and hours are the measurable form of the promise.
senses.whyCN: 当有价值的东西被交出去，承诺就变得具体。金钱与工时就是承诺的可计量形式。

senses.title: Entrust something to someone's care
senses.definition: to hand something over to someone to keep, carry out, or look after
senses.definitionCN: 把某物交给某人保存、执行或照管
senses.example: She committed the documents to her lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把文件托付给了律师。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: something leaves your keeping and enters another's charge. The promise here is made by the receiver, not the giver.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：某物离开你的保管，进入别人的职守。这里的承诺由接收者作出，而不是交出者。

senses.title: Perpetrate a crime
senses.definition: to carry out a crime, sin, or serious mistake
senses.definitionCN: 实施罪行、过失或严重错误
senses.example: He committed fraud over a period of three years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在三年间持续实施诈骗。
senses.why: The same 'carry out' idea turns dark: what is committed is not a task given by another but an act the person performs and must answer for.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“办成”的意念转暗：被 commit 的不再是别人交托的任务，而是此人自己完成、并必须为此负责的行为。

senses.title: Send to prison or an institution
senses.definition: to send someone officially to prison or to a psychiatric hospital
senses.definitionCN: 正式将某人送进监狱或精神病院
senses.example: The court committed him to a secure hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把他送入了封闭式医院。
senses.why: Here a person is handed over to an institution's keeping. The state does the committing, and the prisoner or patient is the thing entrusted.
senses.whyCN: 这里人被交给机构保管。实施 commit 的是国家，被托付的则是囚犯或病人。

senses.title: Bind yourself legally
senses.definition: to bind oneself by a formal agreement or statement
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式协议或声明约束自己
senses.example: By signing, they committed themselves to a five-year lease.
senses.exampleCN: 签字后，他们就把自己绑进了五年的租约。
senses.why: The reflexive form makes the promise legally real: the signer is both the one who hands over and the thing handed over.
senses.whyCN: 反身形式让承诺在法律上生效：签字者既是交出的人，也是被交出的东西。

senses.title: Commit code changes
senses.definition: in computing, to record changes permanently in a version-control system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，把改动永久记入版本控制系统
senses.example: She committed the fix with a short message.
senses.exampleCN: 她提交了这个修复，并附上简短说明。
senses.why: A code change is first only local and reversible. Committing hands it over to the shared repository, where it becomes part of the record.
senses.whyCN: 代码改动起初只在本地、可以撤销。commit 把它交给共享仓库，从此成为记录的一部分。

senses.title: Send troops into action
senses.definition: to send soldiers or forces into a battle or operation
senses.definitionCN: 把士兵或部队投入战斗或行动
senses.example: The government committed another brigade to the region.
senses.exampleCN: 政府又向该地区投入了一个旅。
senses.why: Once troops are committed, they cannot be held in reserve. The word marks the point where a force stops being optional and becomes engaged.
senses.whyCN: 部队一旦被 commit，就不能再留在预备队。这个词标记的正是兵力从“可选”变成“已投入”的那一刻。

senses.title: Be committed to a cause
senses.definition: to be loyally devoted to a principle, group, or belief
senses.definitionCN: 忠诚地献身于某项原则、群体或信念
senses.example: She has been committed to public health for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她投身公共卫生事业已二十年。
senses.why: Repeated promises turn into a standing identity. The past participle committed names a person who is held by the cause as much as holding it.
senses.whyCN: 反复的承诺会沉淀成一种长期身份。过去分词 committed 形容一个人既拥护这个事业，也被这个事业所握住。

intro.en: Commit is the verb from Latin committere; commission is the noun from the same verb. The pair split in English, and commit picked up the criminal and computing senses.
intro.cn: commit 是由拉丁语 committere 来的动词，commission 是同一动词的名词。二者在英语中分流，commit 又发展出犯罪与计算机义。

items.en: Committere meant 'to unite, connect, combine; to entrust, commit; to do, perpetrate'. The core is com- 'with' plus mittere 'to send'.
items.cn: committere 意为“连接、联合；托付、交办；做出、实施”，核心是 com-“一起”加 mittere“送出”。

items.en: Commit entered English around 1400 with the sense 'to entrust, give in charge'. This is still the formal sense in 'commit something to someone'.
items.cn: commit 约在 1400 年进入英语，意为“托付、交付掌管”。这仍是 commit something to someone 中的正式义。

items.en: The sense 'to do or perpetrate' appears in the 15th century, first with sins and crimes. The word does not add the wrongdoing; it only names the doing.
items.cn: “做出、实施”这一义在 15 世纪出现，最早用于罪与过失。词本身并不添加“坏”，只是命名“做出”这个动作。

items.en: Commit to prison or to an institution is recorded in the 17th century. Here the state hands a person over to a place of confinement.
items.cn: “收押入狱、送入机构”记录于 17 世纪。这里是国家把人交给一个监禁场所。

items.en: The modern senses of pledging oneself and of committing code are 20th-century developments. The computing sense comes from version control in the late 20th century.
items.cn: 现代“承诺投身”与“提交代码”两义都是 20 世纪的发展；计算机义来自 20 世纪后期的版本控制。

items.en: Commit and commission are doublets. Commission came through Old French as a noun; commit came later as a verb from the same Latin source. Commitment is the native noun for commit.
items.cn: commit 与 commission 是双式词：commission 经古法语以名词身份进入，commit 后来以动词身份出自同一拉丁语源。commit 的本族名词是 commitment。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: a task or authority entrusted to someone. It is the noun twin of commit from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 委托；委员会；佣金。它是 commit 由同一拉丁动词而来的名词双生子。

entries.definition: a promise or dedication. It is the ordinary noun built on commit.
entries.definitionCN: 承诺；投入。它是 commit 的普通名词形式。

entries.definition: a group appointed to handle a matter. It is close in form but names people, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 委员会。词形接近，但指一群人，而不是一个动作。

entries.definition: loyal and devoted. It is the past participle used to describe a person.
entries.definitionCN: 坚定的；忠诚的。它是过去分词作形容词，用来描述人。

entries.definition: to promise seriously, often publicly. It matches commit in its promise sense but is more solemn.
entries.definitionCN: 郑重承诺，常为公开承诺。对应 commit 的承诺义，但更庄重。

entries.definition: to give time, effort, or oneself to a purpose. It stresses the offering rather than the binding.
entries.definitionCN: 献身；把时间精力给某目标。强调“奉献”，而不是“受约束”。

entries.definition: to give something to someone to care for. It matches the oldest sense of commit.
entries.definitionCN: 托付；委托保管。对应 commit 最古老的义项。

entries.definition: to carry out a crime or harmful act. It is the formal word for the criminal sense of commit.
entries.definitionCN: 实施（罪行）。它是 commit 犯罪义对应的正式用词。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin committere, the doublet commission, and the fixed phrases commit a crime, commit to memory and commit changes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 committere、双式词 commission，以及 commit a crime、commit to memory、commit changes 等固定搭配。

normal.en: commit = com- 'together' + mittere 'send': you send your future into a promise.
normal.cn: commit = com-“一起”+ mittere“送出”：你把自己的未来送进一个承诺。

normal.en: Commission is the twin noun: a commission is the task handed over, a commitment is the promise to carry it.
normal.cn: commission 是双生名词：commission 是被交出的任务，commitment 是承担它的承诺。

normal.en: Commit a crime uses the neutral 'carry out' sense: the verb names the doing, and the crime supplies the wrong.
normal.cn: commit a crime 用的是中性的“办成”义：动词只命名行为，“错”由 crime 提供。

normal.en: Commit to memory sends a fact into long-term keeping, like handing a file to an archive.
normal.cn: commit to memory 把一件事送进长期保管，就像把文件交给档案库。

normal.en: A git commit makes local changes part of the shared record: the change stops being private.
normal.cn: git commit 让本地改动成为共享记录的一部分：改动从此不再是私有的。

abstract.en: The core picture is a hand pressed on a contract: once the hand is there, it cannot be used for something else.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一只手按在契约上：手一旦放上去，就不能再拿去干别的。

abstract.en: All senses are forms of irreversible transfer: promise, resources, documents, a person, a code change, troops.
abstract.cn: 所有义项都是“不可逆的交付”：承诺、资源、文件、一个人、一次代码改动、一支部队。

abstract.en: The word can bless or condemn the same act: committing to a cause builds, committing a crime destroys.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能祝福也能定罪：committing to a cause 是建设，committing a crime 是破坏。

examples.en: The council committed itself to cutting traffic in the centre.
examples.cn: 市议会承诺减少市中心的交通流量。

examples.en: He committed the whole speech to memory.
examples.cn: 他把整篇演讲稿都背了下来。

examples.en: Please commit the fix before you leave for the weekend.
examples.cn: 请在周末离开前把修复提交上去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可米特」——可米特把米按在契约上，说定了就不反悔 → commit 承诺、投入

root: 源自拉丁语 committere“托付、交办；做出”，由 com-“一起”+ mittere“送出”构成，核心是“把自己或某物交出去、不再收回”，与 commission 同源。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of commit, all one irreversible transfer: a promise, resources, a document, a crime, a prisoner, a legal bond, a code change, troops, and a lifelong cause.
sensesIntro.cn: commit 的九个义项都是同一次不可逆的交付：一个承诺、一批资源、一份文件、一桩罪行、一个被收押的人、一份法律约束、一次代码提交、一支部队，以及一个终身事业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressed onto a contract, no longer free to be used elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在契约上，不能再拿去做别的。

branches.en: THE PLEDGE: a promise is made once, then lived as a standing commitment to a cause.
branches.cn: 承诺：承诺作出一次，之后作为长期的事业献身被活出来。

branches.en: RESOURCES SENT: money and troops are committed when they leave the reserve and enter the operation.
branches.cn: 资源送出：资金与部队离开预备状态、进入行动，就是被 commit。

branches.en: A THING OR PERSON ENTRUSTED: documents pass to a lawyer, and a prisoner passes to an institution.
branches.cn: 被托付的物或人：文件交给律师，囚犯交给机构。

branches.en: THE DEED DONE: the neutral 'carry out' sense takes on the wrong supplied by its object.
branches.cn: 做出的行为：中性的“办成”义，由其宾语提供“错”的部分。

branches.en: BOUND BY RECORD: a signature binds in law, and a code commit binds a change into the shared history.
branches.cn: 被记录绑定：签字在法律上绑定，代码提交则把改动绑进共享历史。

intro.en: Commit is built from Latin com- plus mittere 'send'. English adds -ment, -al, -ed and -er; the same Latin verb also produced commission, so the two families overlap.
intro.cn: commit 由拉丁语 com- 加 mittere“送出”构成。英语加 -ment、-al、-ed、-er；同一拉丁动词还产生 commission，因此两个词族彼此交叠。

latinIntro.en: Mittere 'to send' is a major Latin root in English: mission, missile, transmit, submit, permit, admit, emit, remit and commit all belong to it.
latinIntro.cn: mittere“送出”是英语中的主要拉丁词根之一：mission、missile、transmit、submit、permit、admit、emit、remit、commit 都属于它。

items.meaning: to entrust, pledge, or carry out
items.meaningCN: 托付；承诺；实施（com- 表“一起”，mittere 表“送出”）
items.example: They committed the case to a senior judge.
items.exampleCN: 他们把这个案子交给一位资深法官。

items.meaning: a promise, or the state of being devoted
items.meaningCN: 承诺；投入；献身（-ment 构成动作或状态名词）
items.example: The project needs a two-year commitment.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目需要两年的投入。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or to a grave
items.meaningCN: 收押；交付审判；下葬（-al 构成名词）
items.example: The committal hearing was set for June.
items.exampleCN: 交付审判的听证定在六月。

items.meaning: devoted, or already carried out
items.meaningCN: 坚定的；已实施的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.example: She is a committed teacher.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位尽职的教师。

items.meaning: not revealing a position
items.meaningCN: 不表态的；含糊其辞的（non- 表否定）
items.example: He gave a noncommittal answer.
items.exampleCN: 他给了一个不置可否的回答。

items.meaning: one who commits, especially code
items.meaningCN: 提交者（尤指代码提交者，-er 表示人）
items.example: The committer added a clear message.
items.exampleCN: 提交者写了一条清楚的说明。

items.meaning: a task or authority entrusted
items.meaningCN: 委托；委员会；佣金（同一拉丁动词的名词形式）
items.example: The commission began its work in May.
items.exampleCN: 委员会五月开始工作。

items.meaning: a sending, or a task one is sent to do
items.meaningCN: 使命；任务（同一 mittere 词根）
items.example: Their mission was to reopen the road.
items.exampleCN: 他们的任务是重新打通这条路。

items.meaning: to send across
items.meaningCN: 传送；传播（trans-“穿过”+ mittere“送出”）
items.example: The tower transmits the signal inland.
items.exampleCN: 这座塔把信号传向内陆。

items.meaning: to send money; to forgive a debt
items.meaningCN: 汇款；赦免（re-“回”+ mittere“送出”）
items.example: He remits part of his salary home.
items.exampleCN: 他把部分工资汇回家。

definition_zh: 交流；传达；传播（疾病）；相通；（宗教）领圣体
definition_en: to share information, ideas, or feelings with others, or to pass something from one to another
core_image: 两个人把同一份消息从一只手递到另一只手，使各自拥有同样的内容
scene: 窗边的光下，两个人用手势比划着同一个故事。 The two signers used their hands to communicate the same story to each other.
sceneCN: 这里 communicate 是「交流、传达」（第 1 个义项：交换信息与想法）；句意：两位手语者用手把同一个故事交流给对方。

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 善于交流的；交际的；传达信息的
交流者；传播者；通信设备
无法传达的；难以言表的

senses.title: Exchange information with someone
senses.definition: to share information, ideas, or feelings with another person
senses.definitionCN: 与他人分享信息、想法或感受
senses.example: The two teams communicate daily by email.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队每天通过电子邮件交流。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to make common'. Communication is not a one-way transfer but a making-shared: after it, two people hold the same content.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为“使共有”。交流不是单向传递，而是“使共同拥有”：交流之后，两个人握有同样的内容。

senses.title: Get in touch and stay in contact
senses.definition: to make contact with someone, especially to pass on news or ask something
senses.definitionCN: 与某人建立联系，尤指传递消息或询问某事
senses.example: Please communicate with us if the date changes.
senses.exampleCN: 如果日期有变，请与我们联系。
senses.why: The making-common needs a channel first. This sense focuses on opening and keeping the line rather than on the content.
senses.whyCN: “使共有”先要有一条通道。这一义强调的是打开并维持这条线，而不是内容本身。

senses.title: Convey a feeling indirectly
senses.definition: of a work, look, or action, to make a feeling or idea reach others without words
senses.definitionCN: （作品、神情或动作）不用语言就让人感受到某种情绪或想法
senses.example: The music communicates a quiet kind of grief.
senses.exampleCN: 这段音乐传达出一种安静的悲伤。
senses.why: What is made common here is not a fact but a feeling. The sender may not even intend it; the work carries the content.
senses.whyCN: 这里被“共有”的不是事实，而是感受。发送者甚至未必有意，承载内容的是作品本身。

senses.title: Transmit a disease or substance
senses.definition: of a disease, substance, or quality, to pass from one person or thing to another
senses.definitionCN: （疾病、物质或性质）从一人或一物传到另一人、另一物
senses.example: The infection communicates easily in crowded rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 这种感染在拥挤的房间里很容易传播。
senses.why: Sharing can be unwanted. A disease is 'made common' between bodies, which is why communicable became the medical adjective for contagious.
senses.whyCN: “共享”也可能是不想要的。疾病在身体之间被“弄成共有”，所以 communicable 成了医学上“可传染的”形容词。

senses.title: Of rooms, to be connected
senses.definition: of rooms or spaces, to be joined so that one opens into another
senses.definitionCN: （房间或空间）相连，一个通向另一个
senses.example: The study communicates with the library.
senses.exampleCN: 书房与图书馆相通。
senses.why: The oldest physical sense: two spaces share a passage. What is common is the opening itself.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的物理义：两个空间共用一条通道。被“共有”的是那个开口本身。

senses.title: Of devices, to exchange signals
senses.definition: of machines or systems, to exchange data or signals
senses.definitionCN: （机器或系统）交换数据或信号
senses.example: The sensor communicates with the controller every second.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器每秒与控制器通信一次。
senses.why: Machines have no intentions, but they do make data common. The word's 'shared' core needs no human mind.
senses.whyCN: 机器没有意图，但确实让数据“共有”。这个词“共享”的内核并不需要人类心智。

senses.title: Receive Communion
senses.definition: in Christian practice, to receive the consecrated bread and wine
senses.definitionCN: 在基督教实践中领受祝圣的饼与酒
senses.example: The congregation communicated at the early service.
senses.exampleCN: 会众在清晨礼拜中领了圣体。
senses.why: Communion is the religious form of 'making common': the worshipper shares in one body. English keeps the verb for that shared participation.
senses.whyCN: communion 是“使共有”的宗教形式：信徒共享同一个身体。英语用这个动词保留那种共享参与。

senses.title: Speak through the body
senses.definition: to express meaning through gesture, posture, or expression rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 通过手势、姿态或表情而非语言表达意思
senses.example: His folded arms communicated that the discussion was over.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱起的双臂传达出讨论已经结束。
senses.why: The channel shifts from voice to body, but the act is unchanged: something inside becomes shared with someone outside.
senses.whyCN: 通道从声音换成了身体，但动作没变：里面的东西被外面的人共享了。

senses.title: Announce something officially
senses.definition: to make a decision or piece of news known to the people concerned
senses.definitionCN: 把决定或消息告知相关的人
senses.example: The board communicated its decision to all staff.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会向全体员工传达了决定。
senses.why: An official communication aims at full coverage: every concerned person must hold the same news, or the making-common has failed.
senses.whyCN: 正式传达追求“全覆盖”：每个相关的人都必须握有同一条消息，否则“使共有”就没有完成。

intro.en: Communicate comes from Latin communicare 'to make common', built on communis 'shared'. The same base gives common, community and communion, so the whole family is about holding something together.
intro.cn: communicate 来自拉丁语 communicare“使共有”，建立在 communis“共享的”上。同一个基干还给出 common、community、communion，整族词都关于“一起握有某物”。

items.en: Communicare meant 'to share, divide out; impart, inform; join, unite; make common'. It was used for sharing goods, news, and even a road.
items.cn: communicare 意为“分享、分给；告知；连接、联合；使共有”，可用于分享物品、消息，甚至一条道路。

items.en: Communis meant 'common, public, shared by all'. Its deeper make-up is disputed: one old analysis is com- 'together' + munia 'duties', another is a prehistoric compound meaning 'shared in exchange'.
items.cn: communis 意为“共同的、公共的、众人共享的”。其更深构成有争议：一种旧分析是 com-“一起”+ munia“职责”，另一种认为是史前复合词，意为“在交换中共享”。

items.en: English borrowed communicate in the 1520s with the sense 'to share or impart'. The 'exchange information' sense grew from that.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪 20 年代借入 communicate，意为“分享、传递”。“交换信息”义由此生长出来。

items.en: The sense of rooms or passages 'communicating' is recorded in the 17th century. It is a physical survival of the old 'shared opening' idea.
items.cn: 房间或通道“相通”这一义记录于 17 世纪，是古老“共用开口”概念的物理遗存。

items.en: Communicable for contagious disease, and communication for transport and signalling, expanded the word into medicine and technology.
items.cn: communicable 指“可传染的”，communication 指运输与通信，把这个词扩展到医学与技术领域。

items.en: If the older analysis is right, the base would be PIE *mei- 'to change, exchange'. Standard references hedge, so the deepest etymology is source uncertain.
items.cn: 若旧分析成立，其基干可追溯到原始印欧语 *mei-“改变、交换”。通行资料对此有所保留，故最深层词源来源不确定。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the exchange of information, or a message. It is the noun built directly on communicate.
entries.definitionCN: 交流；通信；信息。它是直接由 communicate 构成的名词。

entries.definition: a group of people sharing a place or identity. It comes from the same communis 'shared' base.
entries.definitionCN: 社区；共同体。它来自同一个 communis“共享”基干。

entries.definition: a small community sharing property or work. It is close in form and shares the 'common' idea.
entries.definitionCN: 公社。词形接近，也含“共同”之意。

entries.definition: willing to talk and share information. It is the adjective built on communicate.
entries.definitionCN: 健谈的；乐于交流的。它是由 communicate 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: to make an idea or feeling reach someone. It stresses transport of the content, not the shared result.
entries.definitionCN: 传达；运送。强调内容的运送，而不是“双方共有”的结果。

entries.definition: to send information, signals, or disease from one point to another. It is more technical and more one-way.
entries.definitionCN: 传送；传播。更技术化，也更偏单向。

entries.definition: to tell someone facts. It is narrower and more official than communicate.
entries.definitionCN: 告知；通知。比 communicate 更窄、更正式。

entries.definition: to give part of something to others, or to have it in common. It is the plain native word behind the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 分享；共有。它就是那个拉丁动词背后的本族语直白说法。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin communis 'shared', the common/community/communion family, and the fixed phrases communicate with and communicate a message.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 communis“共享”、common/community/communion 词族，以及 communicate with、communicate a message 等固定搭配。

normal.en: communicate = communicare 'make common': after you communicate a fact, two people have it.
normal.cn: communicate = communicare“使共有”：你传达一个事实之后，两个人就都拥有了它。

normal.en: common, community and communion are the same family: all describe something held together.
normal.cn: common、community、communion 是同一词族：都描述“被一起握有”的东西。

normal.en: Communicable disease is 'shareable' disease, which is exactly what contagious means.
normal.cn: communicable disease 就是“可共享”的病，也就是“可传染的”。

normal.en: Rooms that communicate share a doorway, the most literal kind of common space.
normal.cn: 相通的两个房间共用一个门洞，这是最字面意义的“共同空间”。

normal.en: A good communicator makes one message exist in many heads at once.
normal.cn: 好的沟通者能让同一条消息同时存在于许多人的头脑里。

abstract.en: The core picture is a hand passing an object to another hand: before, one holds it; after, two do.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一只手把东西递给另一只手：之前一个人有，之后两个人有。

abstract.en: The object can be a fact, a feeling, a disease, a signal, or a piece of bread; the operation is always 'make shared'.
abstract.cn: 被递的东西可以是事实、感受、疾病、信号或一块饼；操作始终是“使共有”。

abstract.en: Communication fails exactly when the second hand stays empty.
abstract.cn: 交流失败，恰恰发生在第二只手始终空着的时候。

examples.en: Good leaders communicate the reason behind a decision, not just the decision.
examples.cn: 好的领导者会传达决定背后的理由，而不只是决定本身。

examples.en: The two buildings communicate through a covered passage.
examples.cn: 两栋建筑通过一条有顶的通道相连。

examples.en: Some diseases communicate more easily in cold weather.
examples.cn: 有些疾病在寒冷天气里更容易传播。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可谬你凯特」——可谬（谬论）你也能跟凯特说清楚，就是把话传达到位 → communicate 交流、传达

root: 源自拉丁语 communicare“使共有、分享、告知”，出自 communis“共同的”，与 common、community、communion 同源，核心是“把同一份内容变成双方共有”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of communicate, all one operation of making something common: information, contact, a feeling, a disease, a doorway, a signal, a sacrament, a gesture, and an official decision.
sensesIntro.cn: communicate 的九个义项都是同一个“使共有”的操作：信息、联系、感受、疾病、门洞、信号、圣事、手势，以及一项正式决定。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand passes a content to another, so that both now hold it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一份内容递给另一只手，于是两边都握有它。

branches.en: PEOPLE SHARING: two people exchange content, and staying in contact keeps the channel open.
branches.cn: 人之间的共享：两人交换内容，保持联系则是让通道不关。

branches.en: BODY AND ART AS CHANNELS: music and gestures make an inner state common without words.
branches.cn: 身体与艺术作通道：音乐与手势不用语言，就把内在状态变成共有。

branches.en: UNWANTED SHARING: disease is passed from body to body, the dark side of 'common'.
branches.cn: 不想要的共享：疾病在身体间传递，这是“共同”的阴暗面。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN CHANNELS: rooms share a passage, and machines share signals.
branches.cn: 非人通道：房间共用一条通道，机器共用信号。

branches.en: SHARED BODY, SHARED NEWS: worshippers share one bread, and staff share one announcement.
branches.cn: 共有的身体、共有的消息：信徒共享一块饼，员工共享一则通知。

intro.en: Communicate is Latin communicare plus the English verb ending -ate. The base commun- is not a prefix-plus-root construction; it is the Latin adjective communis, and English builds -ication, -icative, -icator and -icable on top.
intro.cn: communicate 是拉丁语 communicare 加英语动词后缀 -ate。基干 commun- 不是“前缀加词根”，而是拉丁形容词 communis；英语在其上构成 -ication、-icative、-icator、-icable。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base communis 'shared' also gives common, community, communion and Communism, as well as municipal through the related munia 'duties'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基干 communis“共享的”还给出 common、community、communion、Communism，以及经由相关词 munia“职责”而来的 municipal。

items.meaning: to make common, share, impart
items.meaningCN: 交流；传达；使共有（communis“共享”+ 动词后缀）
items.example: They communicate through a shared notebook.
items.exampleCN: 他们通过一本共享的笔记本交流。

items.meaning: the act of sharing information; a message
items.meaningCN: 交流；通信；信息（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: Clear communication prevents mistakes.
items.exampleCN: 清晰的沟通能避免错误。

items.meaning: willing or able to share information
items.meaningCN: 乐于交流的；传达性的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: She is unusually communicative.
items.exampleCN: 她格外乐于交流。

items.meaning: one who communicates well; a signalling device
items.meaningCN: 交流者；传播者；通信设备（-or 表示人或装置）
items.example: He is a gifted communicator.
items.exampleCN: 他是一位有天赋的沟通者。

items.meaning: able to be passed on, especially of disease
items.meaningCN: 可传染的；可传达的（-able 表“能够被……”）
items.example: The disease is highly communicable.
items.exampleCN: 这种病传染性很强。

items.meaning: unable to be expressed or passed on
items.meaningCN: 无法传达的；难以言表的（in- 表否定）
items.example: The feeling was almost incommunicable.
items.exampleCN: 那种感受几乎无法言说。

items.meaning: shared by two or more; ordinary
items.meaningCN: 共同的；普通的（同一 communis 基干）
items.example: The two families share a common garden.
items.exampleCN: 两家人共用一个花园。

items.meaning: a group sharing a place or identity
items.meaningCN: 社区；共同体（-ity 构成性质或集体名词）
items.example: The whole community joined the clean-up.
items.exampleCN: 整个社区都参加了清理。

items.meaning: shared participation, especially religious
items.meaningCN: 共享；共融；圣餐（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: They felt a communion with nature.
items.exampleCN: 他们感到与自然融为一体。

items.meaning: relating to a city's local government
items.meaningCN: 市政的（由相关词 munia“公共职责”构成）
items.example: The municipal pool opens in June.
items.exampleCN: 市政游泳池六月开放。

definition_zh: 社区；群体；共同体；（生物）群落；共有
definition_en: a group of people who live in one place or share an identity, or a group of living things in one habitat
core_image: 一圈人围坐在一起，把各自的资源放进同一个公共的筐里
scene: 周末，邻居们提着食物袋走进社区中心。 At the weekend the neighbours put their food into the same shared fridge at the community centre.
sceneCN: 这里 community 是「社区」（第 1 个义项：居住在同一地区并共享设施的人群）；句意：周末，邻居们把食物放进社区中心的同一个共享冰箱。

pos.zh: 社区；群体；共同体；群落；共有

derivatives.zh: 公共的；共有的；社区共享的
社群主义的；共同体取向的
社群主义；（南亚）教派对立

senses.title: People living in one area
senses.titleCN: 居住在同一地区的人群
senses.definition: a group of people who live in the same area and share local services
senses.definitionCN: 居住在同一地区、共用地方服务的一群人
senses.example: The whole community turned out for the clean-up.
senses.exampleCN: 整个社区的人都出来参加清理。
senses.why: The Latin base communis means 'shared'. A community is first the people who share a place, and with it the roads, schools and problems of that place.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁基干 communis 意为“共享的”。community 首先指共享一个地方的人，以及随之共享的道路、学校与问题。

senses.title: A group with a shared identity
senses.titleCN: 共享身份或兴趣的群体
senses.definition: a group of people who share a religion, origin, interest, or way of life
senses.definitionCN: 共享宗教、出身、兴趣或生活方式的一群人
senses.example: The city has a large Greek community.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市有一个很大的希腊裔社群。
senses.why: The shared thing need not be land. What makes the group a community is a common identity strong enough to organise life around.
senses.whyCN: 被共享的不一定是土地。让一个群体成为 community 的，是强到足以组织生活的共同身份。

senses.title: The public beyond one's group
senses.titleCN: 个人所属群体之外的公众
senses.definition: the wider public or society, especially in phrases such as 'in the community'
senses.definitionCN: 更广的公众或社会，尤见于 in the community 等短语
senses.example: The clinic serves people living in the community.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所服务的是社区里的居民。
senses.why: Institutional language contrasts 'inside' with 'outside': patients in hospital versus people in the community. The word marks ordinary shared life.
senses.whyCN: 机构语言用“院内”对“院外”：住院病人对 community 里的普通人。这个词标记的是日常的共同生活。

senses.title: A religious or political body
senses.definition: a body of people united by a common faith, rule, or political idea
senses.definitionCN: 由共同信仰、规则或政治理念联合起来的一群人
senses.example: The monks formed a self-supporting community.
senses.exampleCN: 这些修士组成了一个自给自足的共同体。
senses.why: Here the shared thing is a rule of life. The group does not merely live near each other; it holds property and obligations in common.
senses.whyCN: 这里共享的是一套生活规则。这群人不只是住得近，还共同持有财产与义务。

senses.title: An ecological community
senses.definition: a group of different species living together in one habitat and interacting
senses.definitionCN: 在同一栖息地共同生活并相互作用的不同物种
senses.example: A coral reef supports a rich community of fish and plants.
senses.exampleCN: 珊瑚礁养育着丰富的鱼类与植物群落。
senses.why: Biology extends 'shared place' beyond humans. Species that share a habitat form a community because their lives affect one another.
senses.whyCN: 生物学把“共享地点”越出人类。共享栖息地的物种构成群落，因为它们的生存彼此影响。

senses.title: An online community
senses.definition: a group of people who interact regularly on a digital platform around a shared interest
senses.definitionCN: 在数字平台上围绕共同兴趣定期互动的一群人
senses.example: The forum grew into a community of thousands.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论坛发展成了数千人的社群。
senses.why: The shared space is now a platform rather than a street. Regular interaction, not proximity, does the work of holding the group together.
senses.whyCN: 共享空间现在是一个平台而不是一条街。把群体维系起来的是定期互动，而不是地理邻近。

senses.title: Shared ownership
senses.definition: the legal or economic state of being owned or held in common
senses.definitionCN: 被共同拥有或持有的法律或经济状态
senses.example: The land is held as community property.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地作为共有财产持有。
senses.why: The adjective communal keeps the oldest legal sense: what belongs to no single member belongs to all of them together.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 communal 保留了最古老的法律义：不属于任何单个成员的东西，属于全体成员共同所有。

senses.title: A feeling of belonging
senses.definition: the emotional experience of being connected to and accepted by a group
senses.definitionCN: 与一个群体相连、被其接纳的情感体验
senses.example: The small school creates a strong sense of community.
senses.exampleCN: 这所小学校营造出很强的归属感。
senses.why: A community can be felt as well as counted. This sense names the inside view: the group exists as a warmth in its members.
senses.whyCN: community 不仅可以被清点，也可以被感受。这一义命名的是内部视角：群体作为一股暖意存在于成员心中。

senses.title: The international community
senses.definition: the nations of the world regarded as a group with shared rules and responsibilities
senses.definitionCN: 被视为共享规则与责任的世界各国
senses.example: The international community condemned the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 国际社会谴责了这次袭击。
senses.why: The phrase treats states as members of one group, with common norms. It is the word's 'shared' logic scaled up to the globe.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把各国当作同一个群体的成员，共享规范。这是 community 的“共享”逻辑放大到全球尺度。

intro.en: Community is the noun of communis 'shared', and a close relative of communicate. Its history moves from 'fellowship' to 'people of one district' to 'any group with something in common'.
intro.cn: community 是 communis“共享的”的名词，也是 communicate 的近亲。它的历史从“情谊共同体”走到“一个地区的居民”，再到“任何共有某物的群体”。

items.en: Communitas meant 'community, fellowship, society'. It was built on communis 'common, shared', the same adjective behind communicate.
items.cn: communitas 意为“共同体、情谊、社会”，建立在 communis“共同的、共享的”上，也就是 communicate 背后的同一个形容词。

items.en: Old French comunete carried the word with the sense of a body of people living under common rules.
items.cn: 古法语 comunete 承载这个词，指在同一规则下生活的一群人。

items.en: English borrowed community in the 14th century. Early uses were about shared status and common possession as much as about place.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪借入 community。早期用法既关于地点，也同样关于共同身份与共同财产。

items.en: The sense 'people of a particular district' is recorded in the late 14th century. The wider sense 'group sharing a characteristic' develops later.
items.cn: “某一地区的居民”这一义记录于 14 世纪后期；更宽的“共享某特征的群体”义后来才发展出来。

items.en: Ecological community and international community are modern extensions. Online community is a late-20th-century addition.
items.cn: 生态群落与国际社会都是现代延伸；网络社群则是 20 世纪后期的新增用法。

items.en: Modern English uses community for neighbourhoods, identity groups, professions, species, platforms and global society. The constant is a shared something.
items.cn: 现代英语用 community 指邻里、身份群体、行业、物种、平台与全球社会。不变的是“有某样东西被共享”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: to share information. It comes from the same communis 'shared' base, but names an action.
entries.definitionCN: 交流；传达。同出 communis“共享”基干，但它是动词。

entries.definition: a small group living together and sharing property. It is a narrower, often intentional, community.
entries.definitionCN: 公社；共同生活群体。范围更窄，常指有意建立的共同体。

entries.definition: shared by a group. It is the adjective built on community.
entries.definitionCN: 公共的；共有的。它是由 community 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: a political system based on common ownership. It shares the Latin communis base.
entries.definitionCN: 共产主义。它共享拉丁 communis 基干。

entries.definition: the whole system of people living together under shared institutions. It is wider and more abstract than community.
entries.definitionCN: 社会。比 community 更宽、更抽象，强调制度整体。

entries.definition: the area around where you live, and its people. It is strictly local and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 邻里；街区。严格限于本地与物理空间。

entries.definition: a set of people or things together. It is neutral and needs no shared identity.
entries.definitionCN: 群体；一组。中性词，不要求共同身份。

entries.definition: ordinary people seen as a whole. It stresses openness rather than belonging.
entries.definitionCN: 公众。强调公开性，而不是归属感。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin communitas and communis, the communicate family, and the fixed phrases local community and international community.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 communitas 与 communis、communicate 词族，以及 local community、international community 等固定搭配。

normal.en: community and communicate share communis: a community is a group that already has something in common.
normal.cn: community 与 communicate 共享 communis：一个 community 就是已经共有某物的群体。

normal.en: Communal property is the legal core: what no single member owns belongs to all of them.
normal.cn: communal property 是法律内核：没有任何单个成员拥有的东西，属于全体成员。

normal.en: A sense of community is the inside view: the group exists as a feeling of belonging.
normal.cn: a sense of community 是内部视角：群体作为一种归属感存在。

normal.en: An online community replaces the street with a platform, but keeps regular contact as its glue.
normal.cn: 网络社群用平台取代街道，但把“定期互动”保留为黏合剂。

normal.en: The international community applies the same word to states sharing norms.
normal.cn: the international community 把同一个词用到共享规范的国家上。

abstract.en: The core picture is a shared basket: each member puts something in and may take something out.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一个公共的筐：每个成员放进去一点，也可以取走一点。

abstract.en: The shared content can be land, blood, faith, interest, water, or a server; the form of the group follows what is held.
abstract.cn: 被共享的可以是土地、血缘、信仰、兴趣、水源或一台服务器；群体的形态随“共享之物”而定。

abstract.en: Community is both countable and felt: it can be a body of people and a warmth inside them.
abstract.cn: community 既可清点也可感受：它既是一群人，也是他们心里的一股暖意。

examples.en: The library runs evening classes for the local community.
examples.cn: 图书馆为当地社区开设夜校课程。

examples.en: Scientists studied how the community of insects changed after the fire.
examples.cn: 科学家研究了火灾之后昆虫群落的变化。

examples.en: Members of the online community share recipes and gardening tips.
examples.cn: 这个网络社群的成员分享食谱和园艺技巧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可谬内地」——可谬（谬论）也能在内地一方水土里聚成一圈人 → community 社区、共同体

root: 源自拉丁语 communitas“共同体、情谊”，出自 communis“共同的、共享的”，与 communicate、common、communion 同源，核心是“共享同一片地方或同一种身份的一群人”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of community, all one shared something: a place, an identity, ordinary public life, a rule of life, a habitat, a platform, common property, a feeling of belonging, and the society of states.
sensesIntro.cn: community 的九个义项都围绕“某样被共享的东西”：一个地方、一种身份、日常公共生活、一套生活规则、一个栖息地、一个平台、共同财产、归属感，以及国家间的社会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a circle of people around one shared basket, each putting in and taking out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈人围着一个公共的筐，各自放进去、也各自取走。

branches.en: LOCAL LIFE: neighbours, the public outside institutions, and the warmth of belonging are three views of one district.
branches.cn: 本地生活：邻里、机构外的公众、归属的暖意，是同一个街区的三种视角。

branches.en: IDENTITY GROUPS: an ethnic or interest group and an online forum are held together by something shared rather than by land.
branches.cn: 身份群体：族群或兴趣群体与网络论坛，靠共享之物而非土地维系。

branches.en: COMMON RULE AND COMMON PURSE: a religious body shares obligations, and communal property is owned by all members together.
branches.cn: 共同规则与共同钱袋：宗教共同体共享义务，公共财产由全体成员共同拥有。

branches.en: SHARED HABITAT: different species in one place form a community through interaction.
branches.cn: 共享栖息地：同一地方的不同物种通过相互作用构成群落。

branches.en: SHARED NORMS AT WORLD SCALE: states are treated as members of one community.
branches.cn: 世界尺度的共同规范：各国被当作同一个共同体的成员。

intro.en: Community is Latin communitas with the English noun ending -ity. The base commun- also yields common, communal, commune, communion, communicate and Communism.
intro.cn: community 是拉丁语 communitas 加英语名词后缀 -ity。基干 commun- 还给出 common、communal、commune、communion、communicate、Communism。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family is built on communis 'shared': communitas, communio, communicare, and the related munia 'duties' behind municipal.
latinIntro.cn: 这一拉丁词族建立在 communis“共享的”上：communitas、communio、communicare，以及 municipal 背后相关的 munia“职责”。

items.meaning: a body of people sharing something
items.meaningCN: 社区；共同体（communis“共享”+ -itas 状态名词）
items.example: The island community depends on fishing.
items.exampleCN: 这个岛上社区靠捕鱼为生。

items.meaning: shared by a group
items.meaningCN: 公共的；共有的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The village has a communal well.
items.exampleCN: 这个村子有一口公共水井。

items.meaning: a group living together and sharing property
items.meaningCN: 公社；共同生活群体（拉丁 communia“共有之物”）
items.example: They joined a farming commune.
items.exampleCN: 他们加入了一个农业公社。

items.meaning: in a shared way
items.meaningCN: 共同地；公共地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The land is farmed communally.
items.exampleCN: 这块土地由大家共同耕作。

items.meaning: emphasizing community over the individual
items.meaningCN: 社群主义的；社群主义者（-arian 表示人或形容词）
items.example: He holds communitarian views.
items.exampleCN: 他持有社群主义观点。

items.meaning: organization of life around communities; also sectarian division
items.meaningCN: 社群主义；（南亚）教派对立（-ism 表示制度或主义）
items.example: The town suffered from communal conflict.
items.exampleCN: 这座城镇饱受教派冲突之苦。

items.meaning: to make something common
items.meaningCN: 交流；使共有（同一基干 + 动词后缀）
items.example: They communicate across the fence.
items.exampleCN: 他们隔着篱笆交谈。

items.meaning: shared participation
items.meaningCN: 共享；共融；圣餐（-io 构成名词）
items.example: The meal became a communion.
items.exampleCN: 这顿饭成了一次共融。

items.meaning: shared, ordinary
items.meaningCN: 共同的；普通的（同一 communis 基干）
items.example: They found a common language.
items.exampleCN: 他们找到了共同语言。

definition_zh: 兼容的；相容的；合得来的；可共存的
definition_en: able to exist, work, or be used together without conflict
core_image: 两块形状不同的拼图，边缘正好咬合
scene: 旧电脑屏幕上，新软件的安装进度条走到末尾。 The new software ran on the old computer and the installation bar finished without a problem, so the two were compatible.
sceneCN: 这里 compatible 是「兼容的」（第 1 个义项：设备或软件能一起正常工作）；句意：新软件在旧电脑上顺利运行，安装进度条走完没有问题，说明两者兼容。

pos.zh: 兼容的；相容的；合得来的

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 不兼容的；不相容的；合不来的
不兼容；不相容；性格不合

senses.title: Devices that work together
senses.titleCN: 设备或软件能一起工作
senses.definition: of machines or software, able to be used together without problems
senses.definitionCN: （机器或软件）能一起正常使用而不出问题
senses.example: This charger is compatible with most phones.
senses.exampleCN: 这个充电器与大多数手机兼容。
senses.why: The Late Latin word meant 'able to suffer together'. Two devices are compatible when they can undergo the same signals without breaking each other.
senses.whyCN: 这个晚期拉丁词意为“能一起承受”。两台设备 compatible，就是能共同承受同样的信号而不互相损坏。

senses.title: People who get along
senses.definition: of people, able to live or work together peacefully
senses.definitionCN: （人）能和平相处或共事
senses.example: They were compatible from the first week of training.
senses.exampleCN: 培训第一周起，他们就相处得很合拍。
senses.why: Two temperaments can also be tested for fit. The word moves from machines to people because 'enduring together' is what both need.
senses.whyCN: 两种性情也可以测试是否合得上。这个词从机器转到人，因为两者需要的都是“能一起承受”。

senses.title: Ideas that do not contradict
senses.definition: of ideas, statements, or beliefs, able to be true or accepted at the same time
senses.definitionCN: （观念、陈述或信念）能同时为真或被接受
senses.example: His account is compatible with the physical evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法与物证相符。
senses.why: Claims are compatible when they can stand in one frame without one cancelling the other. Consistency is compatibility in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 两种说法能站在同一个框架里、互不抵消，就是 compatible。一致性就是思想上的兼容。

senses.title: Matching a rule or standard
senses.definition: able to be accepted under a particular rule, standard, or system
senses.definitionCN: 能在某套规则、标准或制度下被接受
senses.example: The design is compatible with the city's safety code.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计符合城市的安全规范。
senses.why: A standard is a shape that everything must fit into. Compatibility here means the object can be admitted without changing the rule.
senses.whyCN: 标准是一个所有东西都必须合进去的形状。这里的兼容，指对象能被接纳，而不必改动规则。

senses.title: Medically compatible
senses.definition: of blood, tissue, or organs, able to be given to a patient without rejection
senses.definitionCN: （血液、组织或器官）能移植给病人而不被排斥
senses.example: The donor's blood was compatible with the patient's.
senses.exampleCN: 捐献者的血与病人相容。
senses.why: The body's immune system decides whether two tissues can coexist. This is compatibility at its most physical: the two must literally live together.
senses.whyCN: 免疫系统决定两种组织能否共存。这是最物理层面的兼容：两者必须真正一起活下去。

senses.title: Not conflicting with a goal
senses.definition: able to be done or held without damaging another aim or duty
senses.definitionCN: 能同时进行或持有，而不损害另一个目标或职责
senses.example: A part-time job is compatible with full-time study.
senses.exampleCN: 兼职与全日制学习可以兼顾。
senses.why: Two commitments are compatible when they can occupy one life without forcing a choice. The test is practical coexistence, not similarity.
senses.whyCN: 两项承诺能占据同一个人生、不必二选一，就是 compatible。检验标准是实际共存，而不是相似。

senses.title: Backward compatible
senses.definition: of a new system, able to work with older versions or equipment
senses.definitionCN: （新系统）能与旧版本或旧设备一起工作
senses.example: The update is backward compatible with last year's models.
senses.exampleCN: 这次更新与去年的机型向下兼容。
senses.why: The new must accept the old without forcing everyone to upgrade. Compatibility becomes a promise across time.
senses.whyCN: 新系统必须接纳旧系统，而不强迫所有人升级。兼容在这里成了一种跨时间的承诺。

senses.title: Romantically well suited
senses.definition: of partners, likely to have a harmonious relationship
senses.definitionCN: （伴侣）有可能建立和谐关系
senses.example: They discovered they were not compatible as partners.
senses.exampleCN: 他们发现彼此作为伴侣并不合适。
senses.why: Long-term partnership is the hardest endurance test. The word's old 'suffer together' core is visible here: shared life has to absorb friction.
senses.whyCN: 长期伴侣是最难的耐力测试。这个词古老的“一起承受”内核在这里看得最清楚：共同生活必须吸收摩擦。

intro.en: Compatible began as a legal and ecclesiastical word meaning 'able to exist together'. Its Latin root is literally 'to suffer with', which is why coexistence, not similarity, is the core idea.
intro.cn: compatible 最初是法律与教会用语，意为“能共同存在”。其拉丁词根字面是“一起承受”，所以核心观念是“共存”，而不是“相似”。

items.en: Compati meant 'to suffer with, endure with'. It was built from com- 'with' plus pati 'to suffer, endure'.
items.cn: compati 意为“与之同受苦、一起承受”，由 com-“一起”加 pati“忍受、承受”构成。

items.en: Compatibilis was formed from compati, meaning 'able to suffer or exist together'. The legal sense was about rights and claims that could stand together.
items.cn: compatibilis 由 compati 构成，意为“能一起承受、能共同存在”。其法律义指可以同时成立的权利与主张。

items.en: French compatible carried the word into wider use, still stressing coexistence rather than resemblance.
items.cn: 法语 compatible 把这个词带入更广的用法，仍强调共存，而不是相像。

items.en: English adopted compatible in the 16th century. Early uses were theological and legal: compatible claims, compatible offices, compatible natures.
items.cn: 英语于 16 世纪借入 compatible。早期用法属神学与法律：相容的主张、可兼任的职位、可共存的性情。

items.en: Technology gave the word its modern everyday home: compatible hardware, compatible software, backward compatible systems.
items.cn: 技术给了这个词现代最日常的归宿：兼容硬件、兼容软件、向下兼容的系统。

items.en: The root pati also gives patient, passion, passive and compassion. Compatible and compassion are close relatives: one endures with things, the other feels with people.
items.cn: 词根 pati 还给出 patient、passion、passive、compassion。compatible 与 compassion 是近亲：前者与事物共存，后者与人共情。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the ability to exist or work together. It is the noun built directly on compatible.
entries.definitionCN: 兼容性；相容性。它是直接由 compatible 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be compared because of similar size or quality. It shares the com- + -able shape but means 'similar enough to compare'.
entries.definitionCN: 可比较的；类似的。同样是 com- + -able 结构，但意思是“相似到可以比较”。

entries.definition: having enough skill to do something. It is close in sound but comes from a different sense of a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 有能力的；胜任的。读音接近，但来自另一个拉丁动词的另一义。

entries.definition: able to do something. It shares the -able ending but comes from capere 'to take'.
entries.definitionCN: 有能力的。同样以 -able 结尾，但来自 capere“拿取”。

entries.definition: in agreement with itself or with something else. It stresses logical fit over practical coexistence.
entries.definitionCN: 一致的；不矛盾的。强调逻辑上吻合，而不是实际共存。

entries.definition: having the same colour, pattern, or type. It stresses resemblance rather than ability to work together.
entries.definitionCN: 相配的；同款的。强调相像，而不是能否一起运作。

entries.definition: able to be used in place of each other. It is a stronger form of compatibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可互换的。它是兼容性的更强形式。

entries.definition: naturally fitting a person or purpose. It is warmer and more personal than compatible.
entries.definitionCN: 很合适的。比 compatible 更温暖、更个人化。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin compati 'suffer with', the pati family of patient and compassion, and the fixed phrase compatible with.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 compati“一起承受”、patient 与 compassion 的 pati 词族，以及 compatible with 这一固定搭配。

normal.en: compatible = com- 'with' + pati 'suffer': two things are compatible when they can endure each other.
normal.cn: compatible = com-“一起”+ pati“承受”：两样东西能互相承受得住，就是兼容。

normal.en: patient, passion, passive and compassion share the same pati root: all involve undergoing something.
normal.cn: patient、passion、passive、compassion 共享同一个 pati 词根：都涉及“经受某事”。

normal.en: Compatible with is the fixed frame: always ask what the thing must coexist with.
normal.cn: compatible with 是固定框架：总要问清楚它必须与什么共存。

normal.en: Backward compatible means the new system agrees to suffer the old one without complaint.
normal.cn: backward compatible 指新系统愿意毫无怨言地“承受”旧系统。

normal.en: Blood compatibility is the bodily test of the same word: two tissues must live together.
normal.cn: 血液相容是同一个词在身体上的检验：两种组织必须一起活下去。

abstract.en: The core picture is two puzzle pieces: different shapes, but the edges meet without force.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是两块拼图：形状不同，但边缘不用使力就能咬合。

abstract.en: Compatibility is not identity: the pieces stay different, and that is why they can fit.
abstract.cn: 兼容不是同一：两块拼图始终不同，正因如此才能拼上。

abstract.en: The test is always coexistence under pressure: signals, temperaments, claims, tissues, schedules.
abstract.cn: 检验始终是“压力下的共存”：信号、性情、主张、组织、日程。

examples.en: The app is compatible with both Android and iOS.
examples.cn: 这个应用与安卓和 iOS 都兼容。

examples.en: Their working styles turned out to be surprisingly compatible.
examples.cn: 他们的工作风格出乎意料地合拍。

examples.en: The new rule is compatible with the existing treaty.
examples.cn: 新规定与现行条约并不冲突。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可派特伯」——可派特伯去对接，两边接口正好合上 → compatible 兼容的

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 compati“一起承受”，由 com-“一起”+ pati“忍受”构成，经中世纪拉丁 compatibilis 与法语进入英语，核心是“能共同存在、互不排斥”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of compatible, all a test of coexistence: hardware, temperaments, claims, rules, blood, schedules, old versions, and long-term partners.
sensesIntro.cn: compatible 的八个义项都是一场“共存测试”：硬件、性情、主张、规则、血液、日程、旧版本，以及长期伴侣。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two differently shaped pieces whose edges meet without force.
core.cn: 核心意象：两块形状不同的拼图，边缘不用使力就能咬合。

branches.en: MACHINES ENDURE EACH OTHER: current hardware and old versions must accept the same signals.
branches.cn: 机器互相承受：新硬件与旧版本必须接受同一套信号。

branches.en: PEOPLE ENDURE EACH OTHER: colleagues and partners are tested by daily friction.
branches.cn: 人互相承受：同事与伴侣要经得起日常摩擦的检验。

branches.en: CLAIMS ENDURE EACH OTHER: ideas must stand in one frame, and designs must fit one rule.
branches.cn: 主张互相承受：观念要站进同一个框架，设计要合进同一套规则。

branches.en: BODIES ENDURE EACH OTHER: tissue compatibility is the physical limit case.
branches.cn: 身体互相承受：组织相容是这一概念的物理极限案例。

branches.en: LIVES ENDURE EACH OTHER: a job and a study schedule must share one day.
branches.cn: 生活互相承受：工作与学业必须共用同一天。

intro.en: Compatible is Latin compati plus -ibilis, the ending that means 'able to be'. English adds -ity and -ly, and negates with in-.
intro.cn: compatible 是拉丁语 compati 加 -ibilis（表示“能够被……”）。英语加 -ity、-ly，并用 in- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pati 'to suffer, endure' is unusually productive in English feeling-words: patient, patience, passion, passive, compassion and compatible all descend from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 pati“忍受、承受”在英语情感词中异常高产：patient、patience、passion、passive、compassion、compatible 都出自它。

items.meaning: able to exist or work together
items.meaningCN: 兼容的；相容的（com- 表“一起”，pati 表“承受”）
items.example: The two systems are compatible.
items.exampleCN: 这两个系统是兼容的。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to coexist
items.meaningCN: 兼容性；相容性（-ity 构成性质名词）
items.example: We tested the compatibility of the parts.
items.exampleCN: 我们测试了这些部件的兼容性。

items.meaning: in a compatible way
items.meaningCN: 兼容地；相容地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The two programs run compatibly.
items.exampleCN: 这两个程序可以兼容运行。

items.meaning: unable to coexist or work together
items.meaningCN: 不兼容的；合不来的（in- 表否定）
items.example: The old driver is incompatible with the new card.
items.exampleCN: 旧驱动与新显卡不兼容。

items.meaning: the state of not being able to coexist
items.meaningCN: 不兼容；不相容（-ity 构成名词）
items.example: They cited incompatibility as the reason.
items.exampleCN: 他们以性格不合为由。

items.meaning: a person receiving medical care; also able to endure
items.meaningCN: 病人；有耐心的（同一 pati 词根）
items.example: The patient recovered quickly.
items.exampleCN: 病人很快康复了。

items.meaning: strong feeling, especially suffering or love
items.meaningCN: 激情；酷爱；受难（同一词根，原含“承受”之意）
items.example: She has a passion for astronomy.
items.exampleCN: 她酷爱天文学。

items.meaning: receiving action rather than acting
items.meaningCN: 被动的；消极的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: He took a passive role in the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 他在会上扮演被动角色。

items.meaning: sympathy for the suffering of others
items.meaningCN: 同情；怜悯（com-“一起”+ pati“承受”）
items.example: She treated the refugees with compassion.
items.exampleCN: 她以同情之心对待难民。

definition_zh: 补偿；赔偿；弥补；抵消；给……报酬
definition_en: to pay someone for a loss, or to balance one effect against another
core_image: 天平一端放损失，另一端放等重的钱或好处，让它重新水平
scene: 客服桌上摊着退款单和运费发票。 The company compensated the customer for the delayed order and refunded the shipping fee.
sceneCN: 这里 compensate 是「赔偿、补偿」（第 1 个义项：为造成的损失付钱）；句意：公司为延误的订单赔偿客户，并退还了运费。

pos.zh: 补偿；赔偿；弥补；抵消；给……报酬

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

senses.title: Pay for a loss
senses.definition: to pay someone money because they have suffered a loss or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因某人遭受损失或伤害而向其付钱
senses.example: The airline compensated passengers for the long delay.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司为长时间延误赔偿了乘客。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to weigh together'. The loss is put on one pan and money on the other until the scales come level.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为“一起称”。损失放在一个秤盘上，钱放在另一个，直到天平重新水平。

senses.title: Make up for a disadvantage
senses.definition: to reduce the bad effect of something by doing something helpful
senses.definitionCN: 通过做有益的事来减轻某事的不良影响
senses.example: Her quick thinking compensated for the lack of experience.
senses.exampleCN: 她的机敏弥补了经验的不足。
senses.why: Not every loss can be paid in cash. Effort, speed, or care can sit on the empty pan and restore the balance.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有损失都能用钱赔付。努力、速度或细心也能放到空着的秤盘上，恢复平衡。

senses.title: Counterbalance an effect
senses.definition: of one force or factor, to cancel or offset the effect of another
senses.definitionCN: （一种力量或因素）抵消另一种力量或因素的作用
senses.example: Higher fuel costs are partly compensated by lower taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 更高的燃油成本被更低的税收部分抵消。
senses.why: The weighing image becomes mechanical: two forces push in opposite directions, and one takes away the other's effect.
senses.whyCN: 称量的意象变得机械：两股力量方向相反，一方抵消另一方的作用。

senses.title: Pay someone for their work
senses.definition: to pay someone for work or services, especially at a good level
senses.definitionCN: 为工作或服务付酬，尤指报酬优厚
senses.example: The firm compensates employees generously for overtime.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为加班给员工丰厚的报酬。
senses.why: Work is a loss of time and energy, and pay is the counterweight. The word treats effort as something that must be balanced.
senses.whyCN: 工作意味着时间与精力的付出，报酬就是配重。这个词把努力当作必须被平衡的东西。

senses.title: Psychological compensation
senses.definition: to try to make up for a felt weakness by excelling in another area
senses.definitionCN: 通过在另一领域出色表现来弥补自感不足
senses.example: He compensates for his shyness by being the loudest in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他靠成为房间里最响亮的人来补偿自己的害羞。
senses.why: The scales are now inside the mind: a felt deficiency is balanced by an exaggerated strength.
senses.whyCN: 天平现在搬进了心里：感到的缺陷，被一种夸张的强项平衡掉。

senses.title: Automatic technical compensation
senses.definition: of a device or system, to adjust automatically so that an error or change is cancelled
senses.definitionCN: （装置或系统）自动调整，以抵消误差或变化
senses.example: The sensor compensates for changes in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器会补偿温度变化带来的影响。
senses.why: A machine can do the weighing continuously: it measures a drift and applies an equal opposite correction.
senses.whyCN: 机器可以持续做这种称量：测出漂移，再施加一个等量反向的修正。

senses.title: Insurance and legal settlement
senses.definition: to make a formal payment that settles a claim or covered loss
senses.definitionCN: 为结清索赔或承保损失作出正式付款
senses.example: The policy compensates homeowners for flood damage.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单为房主赔偿洪水损失。
senses.why: In law and insurance the scales are written into a contract: what counts as loss, and what counts as equal payment, are fixed in advance.
senses.whyCN: 在法律与保险中，天平被写进合同：什么算损失、什么算等额赔付，都事先定好。

senses.title: Offset a weakness by effort
senses.definition: to make up for a shortcoming through extra work or a different strategy
senses.definitionCN: 通过额外努力或不同策略来弥补短板
senses.example: The small team compensated by starting two months early.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小团队靠提前两个月开工来弥补。
senses.why: When the missing weight cannot be bought, it must be produced. Compensation becomes a strategy rather than a payment.
senses.whyCN: 当缺少的重量买不到时，就只能自己造出来。补偿于是从付款变成一种策略。

intro.en: Compensate is a weighing word. Latin compensare meant 'to weigh one thing against another', and every modern sense still puts something on the opposite pan.
intro.cn: compensate 是一个“称量”词。拉丁语 compensare 意为“把一物与另一物放在一起称”，今天每个义项仍是在对面的秤盘上放东西。

items.en: Compensare meant 'to weigh one thing against another, balance'. It was built from com- 'together' plus pensare 'to weigh', a frequentative of pendere 'to hang, weigh'.
items.cn: compensare 意为“把一物与另一物一起称、使之平衡”，由 com-“一起”加 pensare“称重”（pendere“悬挂、称”的反复形式）构成。

items.en: Pendere is the root behind pendant, pendulum, pension and expense: all involve something hanging or being weighed out.
items.cn: pendere 是 pendant、pendulum、pension、expense 的词根：都涉及“悬挂”或“称出”。

items.en: English borrowed compensate in the 17th century. The first sense was 'to be equivalent, make up for'; the money sense came soon after.
items.cn: 英语于 17 世纪借入 compensate。最早的义项是“相当于、弥补”，付钱义随后出现。

items.en: Compensation became a standard word in law, insurance and employment, where a loss or service is matched by a defined payment.
items.cn: compensation 在 19 世纪成为法律、保险与雇佣领域的标准词：损失或服务由一笔确定的款项来对应。

items.en: Psychology adopted compensation for the balancing of a felt weakness, and engineering for automatic correction of error.
items.cn: 心理学用 compensation 指对自感缺陷的平衡，工程学则用指对误差的自动修正。

items.en: Modern usage spans payment, effort, physics, mind and machinery. The unchanged core is a pair of opposite weights brought level.
items.cn: 现代用法横跨付款、努力、物理、心理与机械。不变的内核是一对方向相反的重量被调到水平。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: money paid for a loss, or the act of balancing. It is the noun built directly on compensate.
entries.definitionCN: 赔偿金；补偿。它是直接由 compensate 构成的名词。

entries.definition: serving to compensate. It is the adjective from compensate.
entries.definitionCN: 补偿性的。它是由 compensate 构成的形容词。

entries.definition: to strive against rivals. It shares the com- + -pete shape but means contending, not balancing.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争。同样是 com- + -pete 结构，但意思是争夺，不是平衡。

entries.definition: to examine two things side by side. It is close in sound and also involves pairing, but without the balancing.
entries.definitionCN: 比较。读音接近，也涉及把两样东西并置，但没有“调平”的意思。

entries.definition: to pay someone back money they have already spent. It is narrower and strictly financial.
entries.definitionCN: 报销；偿还。范围更窄，严格限于金钱。

entries.definition: to pay back money or a kindness. It stresses returning what was received.
entries.definitionCN: 偿还；报答。强调把收到的还回去。

entries.definition: to balance one effect with an opposite one. It matches the counterbalance sense of compensate.
entries.definitionCN: 抵消。对应 compensate 的“抵消作用”义。

entries.definition: to do something that corrects a loss or deficiency. It is the everyday phrase for compensating.
entries.definitionCN: 弥补。它是 compensate 最日常的说法。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin pensare 'weigh', the pendant/pension family, and the fixed frame compensate for.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 pensare“称重”、pendant/pension 词族，以及 compensate for 这一固定框架。

normal.en: compensate = com- 'together' + pensare 'weigh': the loss and the payment are put on the same scales.
normal.cn: compensate = com-“一起”+ pensare“称”：损失与赔付被放上同一架天平。

normal.en: pension and pendulum share the pendere root: both hang from something, just as a weight hangs from a scale.
normal.cn: pension 与 pendulum 共享 pendere 词根：都“悬挂”在某处，正如秤砣挂在秤上。

normal.en: Compensate for is the frame for non-money balancing: experience, speed or care can fill the other pan.
normal.cn: compensate for 是非金钱平衡的框架：经验、速度或细心都能填进另一个秤盘。

normal.en: Workers are compensated because hours are a weight taken out of their lives.
normal.cn: 员工获得 compensation，因为工时是从他们生命里取走的一份重量。

normal.en: A thermostat compensates for cold by adding heat, an automatic version of the same balancing act.
normal.cn: 恒温器通过加热来补偿寒冷，是同一个平衡动作的自动版本。

abstract.en: The core picture is a balance beam: one side drops when something is lost, and the other side must be loaded until it rises.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一根天平横梁：一边因损失而下沉，另一边必须加载直到它升回水平。

abstract.en: The counterweight can be money, effort, time, attention, or a machine's correction; the relation is always equal and opposite.
abstract.cn: 配重可以是金钱、努力、时间、注意力，或机器的修正；关系始终是等量反向。

abstract.en: Compensation is therefore both an apology and a physics: it restores a balance that was disturbed.
abstract.cn: 所以补偿既是一种道歉，也是一种物理：它恢复被打破的平衡。

examples.en: The insurance company compensated the family for the damage.
examples.cn: 保险公司就损失赔偿了这家人。

examples.en: Nothing can compensate for the loss of a friend.
examples.cn: 失去朋友是任何东西都无法弥补的。

examples.en: The system compensates automatically when the pressure drops.
examples.cn: 压力下降时，系统会自动补偿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康盆塞特」——康盆里塞进特制的配重，天平立刻平了 → compensate 补偿、抵消

root: 源自拉丁语 compensare“把一物与另一物一起称、使之平衡”，由 com-“一起”+ pensare“称重”（pendere“悬挂、称”）构成，核心是“用等量反向的东西把失衡调平”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of compensate, all a balancing act: a payment for loss, an effort that fills a gap, a force that cancels another, pay for work, a psychological counterweight, an automatic correction, an insurance settlement, and a strategy against weakness.
sensesIntro.cn: compensate 的八个义项都是同一场平衡：为损失付款、用努力填补缺口、以一股力量抵消另一股、为工作付酬、心理配重、自动修正、保险赔付，以及针对短板的策略。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with a loss on one pan and a counterweight on the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，一端放损失，另一端放配重。

branches.en: MONEY ON THE OTHER PAN: damages and insurance settlements put cash against a measured loss.
branches.cn: 另一端放钱：损害赔偿与保险赔付，用现金对冲可计量的损失。

branches.en: EFFORT ON THE OTHER PAN: care, speed or early work can fill a gap that money cannot.
branches.cn: 另一端放努力：细心、速度或提前开工，能填上金钱填不了的缺口。

branches.en: FORCE AGAINST FORCE: taxes, temperatures and pressures can cancel one another.
branches.cn: 力对力：税收、温度与压力都可以互相抵消。

branches.en: PAY FOR TIME: wages are the counterweight for hours taken from a life.
branches.cn: 为时间付酬：工资是从生命里取走的工时的配重。

branches.en: INSIDE THE MIND AND THE MACHINE: a felt weakness is balanced by a strength, and a sensor balances a drift.
branches.cn: 心与机器内部：自感的弱项由强项平衡，传感器则平衡漂移。

intro.en: Compensate is Latin compensare plus -ate. English builds compensation, compensatory, compensator and compensable; the negated or excessive forms are made with over-.
intro.cn: compensate 是拉丁语 compensare 加 -ate。英语构成 compensation、compensatory、compensator、compensable；过度形式则用 over-。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root pendere 'to hang, weigh' also gives pendant, pendulum, pension, expense and spend, all built on the image of something hanging or being weighed out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 pendere“悬挂、称”还给出 pendant、pendulum、pension、expense、spend，都建立在“悬挂或称出”的意象上。

items.meaning: to weigh against, balance, make up for
items.meaningCN: 补偿；抵消（com- 表“一起”，pensare 表“称”）
items.example: The company compensated the delay with a voucher.
items.exampleCN: 公司用代金券补偿了这次延误。

items.meaning: payment for loss; the act of balancing
items.meaningCN: 赔偿；补偿；报酬（-ion 构成动作名词）
items.example: She received compensation for the injury.
items.exampleCN: 她因受伤获得了赔偿。

items.meaning: serving to make up for something
items.meaningCN: 补偿性的（-ory 构成形容词）
items.example: The body has a compensatory mechanism.
items.exampleCN: 身体有一套代偿机制。

items.meaning: one that compensates; an adjusting device
items.meaningCN: 补偿者；补偿器（-or 表示人或装置）
items.example: The compensator keeps the beam level.
items.exampleCN: 补偿器让横梁保持水平。

items.meaning: able to be compensated
items.meaningCN: 可补偿的；应赔偿的（-able 表“能够被……”）
items.example: Only direct losses are compensable.
items.exampleCN: 只有直接损失才可获赔。

items.meaning: to compensate more than necessary
items.meaningCN: 过度补偿（over- 表“过度”）
items.example: He overcompensates for his nerves by talking too much.
items.exampleCN: 他因紧张而话太多，属于过度补偿。

items.meaning: a regular payment made on retirement
items.meaningCN: 养老金；退休金（原指“按量称出、支付”）
items.example: She lives on a small pension.
items.exampleCN: 她靠一笔微薄的养老金生活。

items.meaning: a weight hung so that it swings
items.meaningCN: 钟摆（pendere“悬挂”+ 工具后缀）
items.example: The pendulum swung steadily.
items.exampleCN: 钟摆稳定地摆动。

items.meaning: money spent
items.meaningCN: 费用；开支（ex-“出”+ pendere“称出、支付”）
items.example: Travel is a major expense.
items.exampleCN: 差旅是一项主要开支。

items.structure: Old English spendan, from Latin expendere
items.meaning: to pay out money or time
items.meaningCN: 花费（金钱或时间，同一 pendere 词族的本族化形式）
items.example: They spent the afternoon repairing the fence.
items.exampleCN: 他们花了一下午修篱笆。

definition_zh: 竞争；比赛；争夺；可与……媲美
definition_en: to try to win or do better than others, or to be able to rival them
core_image: 几条船朝同一个浮标划去，只有一条能先到
scene: 六名跑者站在同一起跑线，号码布别在胸前。 Six runners stood at the same starting line and competed for one place in the final.
sceneCN: 这里 compete 是「比赛、竞争」（第 1 个义项：参加竞赛争取胜出）；句意：六名跑者站在同一起跑线上，为一个决赛名额竞争。

collocations.zh: 打价格战；在价格上竞争

forms.label: 过去分词（动词，完成／被动）

derivatives.zh: 竞争的；有竞争力的；好胜的
有竞争力地；以竞争方式

senses.title: Take part in a contest
senses.definition: to take part in a race, game, or other contest
senses.definitionCN: 参加赛跑、比赛或其他竞赛
senses.example: She will compete in the 400 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她将参加 400 米比赛。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to seek together'. Several people aim at one prize, so their seeking becomes a contest.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为“一起追寻”。几个人瞄准同一个奖赏，于是各自的追寻变成一场竞赛。

senses.title: Rival for customers
senses.definition: of companies or sellers, to try to win the same buyers
senses.definitionCN: （公司或卖家）努力争取同一批买家
senses.example: Three supermarkets compete for the same neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 三家超市争夺同一个街区。
senses.why: The prize is not a medal but a customer. Business competition is the same 'seeking together', with money as the finish line.
senses.whyCN: 奖赏不是奖牌而是顾客。商业竞争仍是同一种“一起追寻”，只是终点线换成了钱。

senses.title: Compete for a position
senses.definition: to try to be chosen for a job, place, or limited opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 努力被选中获得工作、名额或有限机会
senses.example: Hundreds competed for the single scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 数百人争夺这一份奖学金。
senses.why: A position is a scarce thing that several people seek at once. The word marks the scarcity that turns seeking into rivalry.
senses.whyCN: 职位是稀缺之物，几个人同时追寻它。这个词标记的正是把“追寻”变成“争夺”的稀缺性。

senses.title: Compete for attention
senses.definition: of ideas, activities, or demands, to vie for the same limited attention or resources
senses.definitionCN: （想法、活动或需求）争夺同样有限的注意力或资源
senses.example: Advertisements compete for a few seconds of your attention.
senses.exampleCN: 广告争夺你几秒钟的注意力。
senses.why: Attention and budget are finite, so anything that wants them is in the same race. The competitors need not be people.
senses.whyCN: 注意力与预算都是有限的，所以任何想要它们的东西都在同一场比赛里。竞争者不一定非得是人。

senses.title: Be able to rival something
senses.definition: to be good enough to be compared with something else, especially in negative sentences
senses.definitionCN: 好到可以与某物相比，尤用于否定句
senses.example: No local restaurant can compete with that view.
senses.exampleCN: 当地没有一家餐馆能比得上那片景色。
senses.why: Here no one is trying to win; the question is whether a thing can even enter the contest. 'Cannot compete' means it is out of its class.
senses.whyCN: 这里没人在努力争胜，问题只是某物能否进入这场比赛。cannot compete 意思是“不在一个级别”。

senses.title: Organisms compete for resources
senses.definition: of living things, to contend for the same food, space, or light
senses.definitionCN: （生物）争夺同样的食物、空间或阳光
senses.example: Young trees compete for light in a crowded forest.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的森林里，幼树争夺阳光。
senses.why: Biology removes the intention and keeps the structure: limited resources, several seekers, one outcome.
senses.whyCN: 生物学抽掉了意图，只留下结构：资源有限、追寻者众多、结果只有一个。

senses.title: Contest an election
senses.definition: to run against others for a political office
senses.definitionCN: 与他人角逐政治职位
senses.example: Two independents competed for the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 两名独立候选人在争夺这个席位。
senses.why: A seat is the prize, voters are the judges, and the campaign is the race. Politics borrows the language of sport.
senses.whyCN: 席位是奖赏，选民是裁判，竞选是赛程。政治借用了体育的语言。

senses.title: Competing claims or theories
senses.titleCN: 相互竞争的主张或理论
senses.definition: used as a participle, describing explanations or demands that cannot all be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 作分词使用，描述不能全部被接受的解释或要求
senses.example: There are competing theories about the origin of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 关于这个词的起源，有几种相互竞争的理论。
senses.why: When two explanations seek the same acceptance, they are competitors even without a prize. This participle is the adjective form of the race.
senses.whyCN: 当两种解释争夺同一份认可，它们就是竞争者，即使没有奖赏。这个分词就是“竞赛”的形容词形式。

intro.en: Compete comes from Latin competere 'to seek together, contend'. Its root petere also gives petition and appetite, and the same verb produced competent, whose earlier sense was 'fit together'.
intro.cn: compete 来自拉丁语 competere“一起追寻、争夺”。其词根 petere 还给出 petition 与 appetite，同一个动词还产生了 competent，其早期义为“合得上”。

items.en: Competere meant 'to go for together, strive after; to be fit or proper'. It was built from com- 'together' plus petere 'to seek, aim at, go to'.
items.cn: competere 意为“共同追求、力争；也指合适、应当”，由 com-“一起”加 petere“寻找、瞄准、前往”构成。

items.en: Petere is the root behind petition, appetite, repeat and centripetal. The core image is reaching toward something.
items.cn: petere 是 petition、appetite、repeat、centripetal 的词根，核心意象是“朝某物伸手”。

items.en: English adopted compete in the 17th century with the sense 'to strive against others'. The spelling and the sports sense settled later.
items.cn: 英语于 17 世纪借入 compete，意为“与他人争夺”。拼写与体育义后来才固定下来。

items.en: The industrial age moved compete into markets: competing firms, competitive prices, competition as an economic force.
items.cn: 工业时代把 compete 推进市场：竞争的公司、有竞争力的价格，竞争成为一种经济力量。

items.en: Ecology and economics extended the word to species and to attention. The participle competing became common for rival explanations.
items.cn: 生态学与经济学把这个词扩展到物种与注意力；分词 competing 常用来形容相互竞争的解释。

items.en: Competent is a doublet: the same Latin verb also meant 'to fit together', which gave competence and competent. Compete is the 'run toward the prize' branch of one verb.
items.cn: competent 是双式词：同一个拉丁动词也表“合得上”，由此产生 competence 与 competent。compete 是同一动词中“朝奖赏奔跑”的那一支。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling, the second for meaning, so that form and sense stay separate.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写挑选，第二组按词义挑选，这样词形和词义不会混在一起。

entries.definition: the act of competing, or a contest. It is the noun built directly on compete.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争；比赛。它是直接由 compete 构成的名词。

entries.definition: skilled enough to do something. It comes from the same Latin verb in its 'fit' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 胜任的；有能力的。它来自同一拉丁动词的“合得上”义。

entries.definition: whole or finished. It shares the com- + plete pattern but comes from plere 'to fill'.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的；完成的。同为 com- + plete 结构，但来自 plere“填满”。

entries.definition: to calculate. It is close in shape but comes from putare 'to reckon'.
entries.definitionCN: 计算。词形接近，但来自 putare“估算”。

entries.definition: to compete or argue for something. It is more formal and more combative than compete.
entries.definitionCN: 争夺；争辩。比 compete 更正式，也更好斗。

entries.definition: to compete eagerly with someone. It is a literary word for the same race.
entries.definitionCN: 激烈竞争。较文雅，指同一场竞赛。

entries.definition: to be as good as someone else. It matches the 'be able to compete with' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 与……匹敌。对应“足以媲美”这一义。

entries.definition: to challenge or compete for something. It is close to compete but often implies disputing a claim.
entries.definitionCN: 争夺；质疑。接近 compete，但常含“质疑某项主张”。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: Latin petere 'seek', the petition/appetite family, and the fixed frames compete with, compete for and compete in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：拉丁语 petere“追寻”、petition/appetite 词族，以及 compete with、compete for、compete in 等固定框架。

normal.en: compete = com- 'together' + petere 'seek': several people seek the same thing at once.
normal.cn: compete = com-“一起”+ petere“追寻”：几个人同时追寻同一样东西。

normal.en: petition and appetite share petere: a petition asks, an appetite reaches, and competing rivals both reach for one prize.
normal.cn: petition 与 appetite 共享 petere：petition 是请求，appetite 是伸手欲求，竞争则是双方都伸向同一个奖赏。

normal.en: Competent is the same verb's other branch: to be competent is to 'fit' the task, not to beat others at it.
normal.cn: competent 是同一动词的另一支：胜任是“合得上”任务，而不是在任务上打赢别人。

normal.en: Compete with is rivalry, compete for is the prize, compete in is the arena. The preposition tells you where you are.
normal.cn: compete with 是对手，compete for 是奖赏，compete in 是赛场。介词告诉你站在哪里。

normal.en: No one can compete with a perfect view: the phrase means the thing is outside the contest altogether.
normal.cn: no one can compete with a perfect view 意思是那东西根本不在比赛之内。

abstract.en: The core picture is a single buoy and several rowers: the same target, limited seats.
abstract.cn: 核心画面是一个浮标与几条桨手：同一个目标，有限的座位。

abstract.en: Competition needs scarcity, not hostility: the race exists because the prize cannot be split.
abstract.cn: 竞争需要的是稀缺，而不是敌意：比赛存在，是因为奖赏无法切开。

abstract.en: The word can be softened into 'be comparable': when no one can compete, the contest becomes a measure of class.
abstract.cn: 这个词可以软化成“比得上”：当无人能 compete，竞赛就变成了级别的衡量。

examples.en: Small shops find it hard to compete with large chains.
examples.cn: 小店很难与大型连锁店竞争。

examples.en: Ten finalists will compete for the prize on Saturday.
examples.cn: 十名决赛选手将于周六争夺这项奖。

examples.en: The two explanations compete for the same evidence.
examples.cn: 这两种解释在争夺同一批证据的支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可比特」——可比特（特别）能跑，才有资格上场跟人争 → compete 竞争、比赛

root: 源自拉丁语 competere“一起追寻、争夺”，由 com-“一起”+ petere“寻找、瞄准”构成，核心是“多人同时朝同一个目标伸手”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of compete, all one race toward a scarce thing: a medal, customers, a job, attention, a standard of quality, sunlight, a seat, and acceptance for an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: compete 的八个义项都是朝稀缺之物奔跑的同一场比赛：奖牌、顾客、职位、注意力、质量水准、阳光、席位，以及一种解释能否被接受。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several rowers heading for one buoy, with only one place at the finish.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条桨手朝同一个浮标划去，终点只有一个位置。

branches.en: THE FORMAL RACE: a sport or an election has rules, judges and a declared winner.
branches.cn: 正式竞赛：体育或选举有规则、裁判与明确胜者。

branches.en: SCARCE PRIZES: customers and jobs are limited, so seeking becomes rivalry.
branches.cn: 稀缺奖赏：顾客与职位有限，追寻因此变成争夺。

branches.en: ATTENTION AS PRIZE: advertisements and ideas race for a few seconds of the mind.
branches.cn: 注意力作奖赏：广告与想法争夺头脑里的几秒钟。

branches.en: THE LIMIT OF RIVALRY: 'cannot compete' means the thing is outside the contest's class.
branches.cn: 竞争的边界：cannot compete 指某物根本不在这个级别里。

branches.en: NO INTENTION NEEDED: trees and theories can compete without wanting to win.
branches.cn: 无需意图：树木与理论都可以竞争，却并不想赢。

intro.en: Compete is Latin competere with the English verb ending -e. Its family runs through -ition, -itive, -itor and -itiveness; the same verb also gives competent and competence by a different sense.
intro.cn: compete 是拉丁语 competere 加英语动词词尾。其词族经由 -ition、-itive、-itor、-itiveness 展开；同一动词还由另一义给出 competent 与 competence。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root petere 'to seek, aim at' gives petition, appetite, repeat and centripetal. Competere adds the com- 'together' idea, which is what turns seeking into rivalry.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 petere“寻找、瞄准”给出 petition、appetite、repeat、centripetal。competere 加上 com-“一起”，正是这一点把“追寻”变成“争夺”。

items.meaning: to seek the same thing as others
items.meaningCN: 竞争；比赛（com- 表“一起”，petere 表“追寻”）
items.example: They compete for the same clients.
items.exampleCN: 他们争夺同一批客户。

items.meaning: the act of competing; a contest
items.meaningCN: 竞争；比赛（-ition 构成动作名词）
items.example: The competition was fierce.
items.exampleCN: 竞争非常激烈。

items.meaning: relating to competition; able to win
items.meaningCN: 竞争的；有竞争力的（-itive 构成形容词）
items.example: Their prices are competitive.
items.exampleCN: 他们的价格有竞争力。

items.meaning: one who competes
items.meaningCN: 竞争者；参赛者（-itor 表示人）
items.example: Each competitor wore a number.
items.exampleCN: 每位参赛者都戴着号码。

items.meaning: in a competitive way
items.meaningCN: 有竞争力地；以竞争方式（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: The league is played competitively.
items.exampleCN: 这个联赛以竞争方式进行。

items.meaning: the ability to compete
items.meaningCN: 竞争力（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The report measures economic competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告衡量经济竞争力。

items.meaning: having enough skill; legally capable
items.meaningCN: 胜任的；有法定资格的（同一拉丁动词的“合得上”义）
items.example: She is a competent driver.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位合格的司机。

items.meaning: the ability to do something well
items.meaningCN: 能力；胜任（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: He showed real competence in the role.
items.exampleCN: 他在这个职位上表现出真正的能力。

items.meaning: a formal request
items.meaningCN: 请愿；申请（同一 petere 词根）
items.example: They signed a petition for a new park.
items.exampleCN: 他们签署请愿书，要求新建一座公园。

items.meaning: a desire for food or something else
items.meaningCN: 食欲；欲望（ad-“朝向”+ petere“追寻”）
items.example: The walk gave them a healthy appetite.
items.exampleCN: 这趟步行让他们胃口大开。

latinEntries.meaning: to strive after together; to be fit
to seek, aim at, go toward

definition_zh: 复杂的；复合的；建筑群；综合体；情结
definition_en: made of many connected parts, or a whole formed from such parts
core_image: 许多线交织成一个结，抽掉一根整块就会散
scene: 园区平面图上，多栋相连的楼由穿梭通道串起。 The hospital was a huge complex, with the clinic, the wards, and the laboratories all in one park.
sceneCN: 这里 complex 是「建筑群、园区」（第 5 个义项：由多栋相互关联的建筑组成的整体）；句意：这座医院是一个巨大的建筑群，门诊、病房和实验室都在同一片园区里。

pos.zh: 建筑群；综合体；情结；复合体

forms.label: 比较级（更多用 more 构成）
最高级（更多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 肤色；面色；（事物的）性质（同出拉丁 complexio）

senses.title: Made of many connected parts
senses.titleCN: 由许多相互关联的部分组成
senses.definition: consisting of many parts that are connected and affect one another
senses.definitionCN: 由许多相互连接、彼此影响的部分组成
senses.example: The human brain is a complex organ.
senses.exampleCN: 人脑是一个复杂的器官。
senses.why: The Latin word means 'woven together'. A complex thing is not merely large; its parts are interlaced, so each part changes what the others do.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词意为“交织在一起”。复杂之物不只是“大”，它的各部分彼此穿插，因此每一部分都会改变其他部分的运作。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: difficult to understand because many things are involved
senses.definitionCN: 因为牵涉因素众多而难以理解
senses.example: The case raises complex legal questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个案子提出了复杂的法律问题。
senses.why: Difficulty is the mental effect of interwoven parts. When you cannot hold all the threads at once, the thing feels complex.
senses.whyCN: 困难是“交织”在头脑中造成的结果。当你无法同时握住所有线头，这东西就显得 complex。

senses.title: A complex number
senses.definition: in mathematics, a number with a real part and an imaginary part
senses.definitionCN: 数学中由实部与虚部组成的数
senses.example: The equation has two complex roots.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有两个复数根。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word literally: a number woven from two different kinds of part, real and imaginary.
senses.whyCN: 数学用的是字面义：一个由两种不同部件（实部与虚部）编织成的数。

senses.title: A complex sentence
senses.definition: in grammar, a sentence with one main clause and at least one dependent clause
senses.definitionCN: 语法中指含一个主句和至少一个从句的句子
senses.example: The essay is full of complex sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章里满是从句复合句。
senses.why: Grammar calls a sentence 'woven' when clauses are nested inside one another rather than simply placed side by side.
senses.whyCN: 当从句嵌套在彼此之中、而不是简单并列时，语法学称这个句子为“编织成的”。

senses.title: A group of connected buildings
senses.definition: a group of buildings or facilities built close together and used as one unit
senses.definitionCN: 建在一起、作为一个整体使用的多栋建筑或设施
senses.example: The sports complex includes a pool and three courts.
senses.exampleCN: 这个体育中心包含一个泳池和三块球场。
senses.why: Buildings are woven by shared function: separate structures become one complex because people use them as a single place.
senses.whyCN: 建筑因共同功能而“编织”在一起：各自独立的楼，因为人们把当成一个场所使用，而成为一个 complex。

senses.title: A psychological complex
senses.definition: in psychology, a group of connected feelings and ideas that strongly influence behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中指一组相互关联、强烈影响行为的情感与观念
senses.example: He has an inferiority complex about his height.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的身高有自卑情结。
